Paul Scholes notes 'rabbit in headlights' Leny Yoro is not 'Premier League level' - as Nicky Butt claims this Man United side are the 'most unathletic team' in their history with only THREE players able to run at Anfield

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 16:03 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:05 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Former Manchester United midfielder Paul Scholes has become the latest ex-Red Devil to tear into the club's defence, criticising Leny Yoro following his red card in his side's 4-0 defeat by Liverpool.
  • Yoro was sent off less than eight minutes into United's clash with their rivals at Anfield on Sunday, tripping Alexander Isak as he ran in on goal after an error from Matthijs de Ligt.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 16:03 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:05 EST, 23 November 2026.

Former Manchester United midfielder Paul Scholes has become the latest ex-Red Devil to tear into the club's defence, criticising Leny Yoro following his red card in his side's 4-0 defeat by Liverpool.

Yoro was sent off less than eight minutes into United's clash with their rivals at Anfield on Sunday, tripping Alexander Isak as he ran in on goal after an error from Matthijs de Ligt.

He has had a mixed time of things since his £52million move to Old Trafford in 2024, though has been playing in a leaky United defence that has conceded 23 goals in 11 Premier League matches this season – with only Crystal Palace conceding more.

Several different members of United's defence have come under fire this season, and, on Monday, it was the turn of Yoro.

'The Premier League at this minute just looks a little bit too much for him,' Scholes said on The Good, The Bad and The Football, sponsored by Midnite.

In a recent development, he added: 'You know what, he’s come in to a really bad setup defensively now. I think they also made the point yesterday if he went in next to (Virgil) Van Dijk he might look a little bit better but he doesn’t look Premier League level. He looks like a rabbit in the headlights.'.

Paul Scholes (pictured) has suggested Leny Yoro is not yet ready for the Premier League.

Yoro was sent off in the opening minutes of Manchester United's 4-0 defeat by Liverpool.

Fellow former United midfielder Nicky Butt, who played alongside Scholes for United between 1994 and 2004, added: 'If that’s Man United in our day, he’s on loan like a Jonny Evans or a John O’Shea. He’s a great talent that will come good.'.

Scholes, though, wasn't having any of it.

It has been revealed that he replied: 'I’m not sure how much of a great talent he is. I think he has shown a little bit of a sign in the France squad but every time I’ve seen him he doesn’t look at the races. Everything’s happening around him and he’s just a bit, oh, what do I do?'.

United have also faced criticism for their apparent lack of running this season, with eyebrows raised when Youri Tielemans noted in the summer that they didn't do much prior to the campaign getting under way.

It has been revealed that the club rank 17th for distance covered in the top flight this season, with Liverpool, Brentford and Everton below them. The latter two will almost certainly pass them though after their game on Monday.

That, according to Butt, is down to the players.

'We’ve had our say about the players and they’re just not good enough,' he stated. 'It is the most unathletic team I’ve ever seen in Man United.

'I’m going to go through a team and I’m trying to be as honest as I can. Forget the quality for right now. For me, physicality-wise, if you go through a team, the right back, he’s physically OK, but he’s not amazing. De Ligt or Harry, whoever he’s going to play in there, physically not great. Martinez for me is physically not great. You got Yoro who will physically come good.

Nicky Butt (pictured), meanwhile, has criticised the physical ability of many of United's players.

Industry observers note that 'Then I go on to the midfield, none of them are physically good enough. Kobbie can get about the pitch 15-20 yards, but he’s not box to box. Said that numerous times. He’s got a lot of talent. He’s got a lot of things going for him. I think he’s a top player. He ain’t got the legs. He needs to have legs around him but his legs around him at the minute are Bruno and Tielemans - and they can’t run around.

'Look at Mbeumo, I think he’s OK but he’s not going to blow anybody away. I think Cunha can run. So then you look at the whole squad and you’re saying three players can run.

'What I’m getting at there, and it sounds like I’m being a draconian but what you have to do first and foremost when you go to Anfield is to be able to compete physically and they can’t so they have no chance.'.

Which Premier League players are set for yellow card suspensions?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (572 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yeremy Pino is the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow-card suspension.
  • Crystal Palace's Yeremy Pino has become the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow card suspension after accumulating five bookings since the 2026-27 season began.
  • Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash were the first players to receive a ban for collecting five yellow cards before gameweek 19.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yeremy Pino is the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow-card suspension.

Crystal Palace's Yeremy Pino has become the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow card suspension after accumulating five bookings since the 2026-27 season began.

Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash were the first players to receive a ban for collecting five yellow cards before gameweek 19.

Players receive a one-match suspension if they pick up five or more yellow cards prior to the conclusion of their team's 19th league match of the season.

There are now 17 players sitting on four bookings after 11 rounds of matches, meaning they must avoid another yellow card prior to the halfway point of the season to avoid a ban.

Bournemouth have the most players on the brink of a ban, with three players one yellow card away from suspension.

After that date, the threshold increases to 10 yellow cards. Any player reaching that number before the end of their club's 32nd league match of the season will receive a two-match suspension.

From that point, there are further thresholds at 15 and 20 yellow cards.

It has been revealed that for players reaching 15 cautions, they incur a three-match suspension. Punishments for players reaching 20 yellow cards are determined by a regulatory commission.

Those cut-offs do not reset until the end of the Premier League season.

In the Championship, League One and League Two, there are similar thresholds.

However, with those three divisions having 46 rounds of league matches instead of 38, players have to avoid getting 10 yellow cards before the end of the 37th league match in order to not receive a two-match suspension.

In those divisions, the yellow cards are reset at the end of the league season and do not include matches in the play-offs.

The following players have received a one-match ban and will now receive a two-match ban if they reach ten bookings before game week 32:.

Yeremy Pino - Crystal Palace (five yellow cards).

Matt Crooks - Hull City (five yellow cards).

Matty Cash - Aston Villa (five).

If any of the following players receive another Premier League yellow card before the season's halfway point, they will be banned for one match:.

Vitaly Janelt - Brentford (four).

Oli McBurnie - Hull City (four).

Harry Maguire - Manchester United (four).

Pascal Gross - Brighton & Hove Albion (four).

Ethan Ampadu - Leeds United (four).

Oliver Boscagli - Brighton & Hove Albion (four).

Adam Smith - Bournemouth (four).

Marcus Tavernier - Bournemouth (four).

Antonio Silva - Bournemouth (four).

Alexis Mac Allister - Liverpool (four).

James McAtee - Nottingham Forest (four).

Chema Andres - Brighton & Hove Albion (four).

Bradley Barcola - Liverpool (four).

Murillo - Nottingham Forest (four).

The following players will miss their club's next set of fixtures:.

Yeremy Pino - Crytsal Palce (yellow card suspension).

Jean-Philippe Mateta - Crystal Palace (red card suspension).

Igor Thiago - Brentford (red card suspension).

Costinha - Brighton & Hove Albion (red card suspension).

Leny Yoro - Manchester United (red card suspension).

James Tarkowski - Everton (red card suspension).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Alexander Zverev misrepresented the result of his 2024 domestic abuse trial, causing harm to his former partner and the mother of his child, Brenda Patea's lawyer has told DW.
  • The case ended without a verdict after both sides reached an out-of-court settlement.
  • As Zverev's lawyers noted in a statement sent to DW: "The criminal proceedings were discontinued...
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alexander Zverev misrepresented the result of his 2024 domestic abuse trial, causing harm to his former partner and the mother of his child, Brenda Patea's lawyer has told DW.

The case ended without a verdict after both sides reached an out-of-court settlement. Zverev, who won the French and US Open in 2026, is alleged to have told French publication L'Equipe that: "I did everything I could, and my innocence has been proven.".

As Zverev's lawyers noted in a statement sent to DW: "The criminal proceedings were discontinued... without any finding of guilt, and the presumption of innocence remains unaffected.".

However, Zverev's statement has harmed Patea's standing and her career as an influencer, according to her lawyer, Michael Scheele.

Industry observers note that "What she suffered after this interview in L'Equipe was published is nothing but a shitstorm. It's also detrimental to her business," Scheele told DW.

"We still don't know the truth objectively and we have an agreement in which he committed not to talk about the incident and the case at all," he added.

However, in the statement sent to DW, Zverev's lawyers asserted that "there has been no breach of any contractual obligations or violation of Ms. Patea’s personality rights.".

Sources indicate that zverev had made similar comments before. On the day the settlement was reached, the tennis pro spoke to reporters at the 2024 French Open.

According to recent reports, "That's what dropping the case is: That is innocence. They're not going to drop the case if you're guilty at the end of the day," he noted.

The lawsuit, seen by DW, states that Zverev should be subject to "a fine of up to €250,000 ($275,000) to be determined for each instance of violation — and, in the event that such fine cannot be collected, substitute custodial detention of up to six months," should he be found guilty.

Zverev's lawyers reject the allegations.

In a recent development, "Our client will defend himself against the lawsuit. If the statement attributed to him was indeed made in the form alleged, we consider it to be a permissible expression of opinion protected by Article 5(1) of the German Basic Law," they remarked.

"Our client would merely have expressed his personal conviction that he had done everything in his power to refute the allegations made against him and that he considers his innocence to have been confirmed by the outcome of the criminal proceedings. "He is fully entitled to hold and express this view.".

The law firm, Schertz Bergmann, added that: "Unlike the opposing counsel, we intend to conduct these proceedings in court rather than in the press.".

Scheele noted he and his client did not want to go back to court but were frustrated in their efforts to resolve matters in other ways.

It has been revealed that "We went forward writing to him in a polite way, asking him to sign and to declare that he's not going to repeat what he said. And he didn't reply. So we wrote twice more, no reply.

Industry observers note that "That's when we had to decide to go to court, which was not the aim at the beginning. We wanted to avoid it, but we had no other choice.".

Zverev, now resident in Monaco, is currently playing in the season-ending ATP Finals tournament in Turin.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City’s feud with the Premier League following the guilty verdict will dominate their season, but it is now events on the pitch that are proving a genuine concern.

Enzo Maresca has lost three league games in a row and, at the City Ground, there was further evidence of defensive instability, strange team selection and key players underperforming.

Eight games without a clean sheet underlines their vulnerability and Maresca has much to ponder over the international break with his team six points behind leaders Arsenal.

What a response from Nottingham Forest to Oliver Glasner’s brutal “no-compromises” rant last weekend, as the home team secured only the second league win in front of their own supporters this year.

It was a former City player, Liam Delap, who tormented them with two brilliant individual goals to give Glasner what he hopes will finally be lift-off.

"The day that Delap ARRIVES" 🤩 Nottingham Forest regain their two-goal lead! https://t.co/5yk5eIhPhe.

It has been revealed that forest’s £50m record signing was on the 55-man list for Thomas Tuchel’s latest England squad and more performances like this will enhance his chances of senior recognition. It was the archetypal “No 9” performance.

While Forest will hope this proves a turning point in their season, these are certainly worrying times for City.

Marc Guéhi and Josko Gvardiol are both badly out of form and were replaced at half-time with injuries, while it was another alarming evening for goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Despite a brief rally early in the second half, City never looked capable of ending their slump. Even the sight of Manchester United in the bottom three will have done little to cheer their supporters.

It has been revealed that maresca said: “I’m always concerned, even when we win games. We won seven in a row and we have now lost three, so over the break we need to understand what we can do better.

According to recent reports, late last week the UN’s climate conference, COP31, failed to reach a consensus on its headline message. That news came on the heels of the UN acknowledging that the 1.5 ˚C warming limit set out in Paris will be breached. So, it’s easy to feel anxious in a world where it seems that not enough is being done about climate change. But is it possible to overcome such anxiety or even use it?

Industry observers note that in the final episode of Cooked? I open up about my own climate anxiety and discover that there are still things that I can do to battle climate change. And how those small individual actions could potentially lead to more systemic change.

00:00 Can I do anything about my climate anxiety?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England are a seeded side for the Nations League quarter-finals after topping their group.

The draw for the final eight teams in the 2026-27 Nations League will be on Friday, 20 November at 11:00 GMT.

It will take place at Uefa's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland and be broadcast on Uefa TV.

England are the only home nation to have made it to the quarter-final stage, however Northern Ireland's draw against Hungary saw them top Group B2 and secure promotion to League A in the 2028-29 tournament.

Scotland will remain in League B following their third-place finish in Group B1, and Wales face a League A/B relegation play-off in March after being consigned to last place in Group A4.

The Republic of Ireland finished second in Group B3 and so will take part in a League A/B promotion play-off in March.

The winners of groups A1-A4 are seeded for the draw, playing the runners-up of other groups in League A.

England have sealed their place in the last eight as Group A3 winners and could face:.

They cannot face A3 runners-up Spain as teams must be drawn against sides from other groups.

The quarter-finals will be played over two legs during the international break between 25-30 March.

Seeded teams get to play the second leg of their quarter-final at home.

Nations that reach the semi-finals can bid those penultimate matches as well as the final.

The remaining dates for the Nations League are:.

Quarter-finals first leg: 25-27 March.

Quarter-finals second leg: 28-30 March.

Semi-finals, third-place play-off and final: 9-13 June.

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 16:30 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:03 EST, 23 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50million to buy Manchester United out of trouble in the January transfer window.

Pochettino admitted that United are in a relegation battle after a painful 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in his first game in charge left the club second from bottom of the Premier League.

In a recent development, it’s understood the Argentine will have a limited budget well under £50million with United’s hands tied by the league’s newly introduced financial rules. Pochettino is only expected to make two new signings in January, even if one of them is a loan deal.

Sources have not ruled out the possibility of United gambling if there is a genuine threat of the club being relegated for the first time in 53 years, but they would still have to spend responsibly.

The defeat to Liverpool underlined the need for Pochettino to strengthen in central defence, with Brentford’s Nathan Collins emerging as a strong candidate ahead of Calvin Bassey, who is expected to sign a new contract with Fulham, and Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite who is valued at over £70million.

It has been revealed that united also want a left-back after failing to sign cover for Luke Shaw in the summer when they were linked with Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde and Rayan Ait-Nouri of Manchester City. Both those players could be potential targets again.

Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50million to try and fix Manchester United in January.

Pochettino is only expected to make two latest signings in January - pictured: Chief executive Omar Berrada (left) and director of football Jason Wilcox (centre).

Pochettino would also like a new striker after Benjamin Sesko’s shin injury left him short of firepower until the New Year.

Monaco’s Folarin Balogun, who played under Pochettino for the US national team, Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Ivan Toney, the former Brentford centre-forward now playing for Al-Ahli, have all been linked with a move to Old Trafford.

However, Toney’s £500,000-a-week wages put him out of United’s reach, and Leeds are keen to extend Calvert-Lewin’s contract which is worth £180,000-a-week.

Meanwhile, United are appealing to the FA over Leny Yoro’s controversial red card against Liverpool.

Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute at Anfield for a challenge on Alexander Isak on the edge of the penalty box. The Frenchman was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott, and Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s first goal from the free-kick.

However, United insist that Yoro did not deny Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity because goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have reached the ball first.

The club have notified the FA of their intention to appeal in the hope of having Yoro’s one-match ban overturned so he can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Emmanuel Emegha has revealed that he was robbed after Chelsea’s home drubbing by Leeds on Saturday.

Emegha started his first Premier League game as the Blues suffered a heavy 4-1 defeat at Stamford Bridge, but was the victim of theft in the hours following the game.

The Dutch striker confirmed the incident on Sunday, writing on Instagram: “Unfortunately after the game I was robbed. I am okay and thankfully no one was hurt. Thanks for the messages of support.”.

Chelsea sources told The Independent that the club is aware of the theft incident involving Emegha and that he has the full support of the club in this matter.

It is understood that the Metropolitan Police has not yet received a formal report regarding the incident and encourage Emegha to contact the authorities via the appropriate channels to allow an investigation to begin.

Emegha scored his first goal for the Blues against Leeds, brilliantly finishing at the near post to open the scoring in the first half before the tide turned heavily against Chelsea.

Noah Okafor equalised three minutes after Emegha’s striker before later scoring again as Leeds ran away with the game after the break, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brendon Aaronson also netting scoring to condemn Chelsea to a damning loss.

Emegha joined Chelsea from sister club Strasbourg in the summer after a deal was agreed to bring the Dutchman to Stamford Bridge in September 2025.

He scored 31 goals in 73 appearances across all competitions in his three seasons in France before making the switch.

Industry observers note that crystal Palace are playing this season as if afflicted by a curse. They seem to have made a terrible deal, possibly involving a monkey’s paw. As a result, Pierre Sage’s team were able to defend credibly for around 44 minutes of each half, on one condition: They must switch off completely, at least twice per game.

This being the Premier League, those lapses in concentration are usually punished. A mostly compact performance out of possession briefly became as porous as a bath sponge when Liverpool eased into a 2-0 lead, nine minutes after half-time. Florian Wirtz did not even need to finish cleanly to score his first Premier League goal of the season, striding on to an unopposed low cross from Bradley Barcola and killing the match as a contest.

Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz combine to put Liverpool 2-0 up! 🔴 https://t.co/F6sw33FkYZ.

Arguably the same could be said for Wirtz, nearly 18 months since he joined.

Neither left Selhurst Park looking like the world-beaters they did occasionally for their previous clubs. Still, one misfiring attacker creating a goal for another represents progress and all great partnerships must start somewhere. Lennon and McCartney would improve after 1958’s Too Bad About Sorrows.

Recent findings suggest that if there was ever a place for the least-productive expensively assembled attacking group in the league to find form it was surely south London on this Sunday lunchtime. Liverpool came in with two defeats in their previous two but, European trophy aside, it has been a lousy 2026 for Palace.

They have the most defeats of any ever-present Premier League team and began (and ended) the weekend with the worst defensive record. They have conceded twice as many goals from headers as any other team. Even their most loyal fan group has disbanded.

Alexis Mac Allister opened the scoring in gut-punching fashion, after a series of Palace near-misses. Chairman Steve Parish rubbed his face in the directors’ box, in the style of peak-stress era Guardiola. None of this looked good for Sage, who appears on the brink of dismissal, with Thomas Frank his most likely replacement.

Asked if he expected to remain in his job on the other side of the international break Sage said he deemed his prospects “better than you, I think”.

According to recent reports, “We deserved better today,” the Frenchman noted. “But football is not about what you deserve it is about how efficient you are and today we had a lack of efficiency”.

Counter-intuitively, it was Palace’s flashes of promise which suggested the Frenchman might be doomed. There is enough to work with here, and plenty going marginally against Palace to suggest a change in leadership might prompt a turnaround, however unfair it would be on their manager. Yéremy Pino hit the bar, Jorgen Strand Larsen had his composed close-range goal struck from the record by VAR, Daichi Kamada stung Alisson Becker’s palms and the Brazilian saved well again from Adam Wharton’s feathered header.

Isak had his moment in the end, checking back to finish calmly at the end of a counter-attack against a tiring defence. Eight for the season for him and an assist for Wirtz, too, although it was hardly a pass of Molbyesque majesty.

Wirtz tests Henderson with a whipped attempt following Nyoni’s strong run and Munoz’s lay-off. However, the Palace captain makes a simple save.

Munoz tries to dribble away from Lerma, but the Liverpool substitute dives over the Palace man’s outstretched leg. Mac Allister then unnecessarily squares up to Lerma because of his annoyed reaction to Munoz’s simulation. As a result, all three of the aforementioned players are booked.

Palace can’t find a way past Alisson. Osorio drives down the wing and picks out the unmarked Pino, whose shot is smothered by the Liverpool goalkeeper. Lerma latches onto the loose ball, but Alisson is there once again to comfortably gather the Palace man’s ambitious rebound.

Liverpool continue to protect their two-goal advantage and make another forward change as Ngumoha comes on for Gakpo.

Sage makes an attacking change as Nketiah, who scored the winner against Liverpool at Selhurst Park in September 2025, replaces Strand Larsen up top.

In fairness to Palace, you can’t fault their effort. Liverpool are holding firm and the hosts are lacking end-product. Pino then catches Araujo with a late tackle to pick up a needless booking.

Industry observers note that no need to be dramatic, but this does rather feel like the season for Pierre Sage. Losing games you have created the best chances in is a bad look for a manager under pressure, especially in the specific circumstances Palace are displaying. There is enough promise and talent in his team to suggest a different voice could extract more from the group. There is also a dreadful habit of switching off entirely, which might make a chairman wonder if it is time for more of a shouty presence in the dugout. The second Liverpool goal was woeful from a Palace point of view.

Iraola makes a double change as Nyoni and Munoz replace Szoboszlai and Barcola.

Sources indicate that alisson claims Wharton’s cross as Strand Larsen falls on the Liverpool goalkeeper. The Brazilian has been faultless today and looks well on the way to a deserved clean sheet as things stand.

The game has become quite chaotic and Palace’s shape has deserted them. If there’s another goal in this game, then it will be absolutely crucial. The hosts are waiting to craft a notable second-half chance.

Sage makes a change on the hour-mark as Osorio replaces Timber in the game’s first alteration.

Barcola is booked after halting a Palace counter with a forceful challenge through the back of Pino.

That second Liverpool goal has left Selhurst Park very deflated. All the noise is coming from the away fans. Mitchell’s makes a crucial intervention to block Barcola’s cross. Palace look so stretched now.

Recent findings suggest that it’s an excellent team goal as two of Liverpool’s big-money attackers devastatingly combine. Barcola is released down the wing and finds Wirtz with a low, pinpoint cross. The German playmaker then sweeps a composed, first-time effort into the bottom corner, leaving Henderson rooted to the spot. It’s a wonderful finish and credit to Barcola for the assist. Palace are in trouble and have a mountain to climb.

Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz combine to put Liverpool 2-0 up! 🔴 https://t.co/F6sw33FkYZ.

Palace have made a positive start to this second half. They win the ball high up the pitch and Kamada tees up Strand Larsen. The striker has a shooting chance, but his touch lets him down, allowing Jacquet to come across and make a tackle.

It has been revealed that timber slides a pass in behind Jacquet for Strand Larsen to chase. However, Alisson is alert to the danger and rushes off his line to collect possession.

We are back under way at Selhurst Park. Both sides are unchanged at the break. Can Palace find a way back into this contest?

A thoroughly entertaining first half at Selhurst Park comes to a close as Liverpool hold a slender 1-0 lead over Palace thanks to Mac Allister’s 40th-minute header. Palace struck the bar through Pino and had a Strand Larsen goal ruled out for offside, but Liverpool have also looked dangerous going forward and their opener came as no surprise to anyone. To Palace’s credit, they’ve really taken the game to Liverpool so far, forcing Alisson into a couple of notable saves. However, there was still boos at half-time and Sage has work to do.

Much fury and gnashing of teeth towards the referee Tony Harrington at half time. The tunnel entrance takes players and officials past some of Palace’s most vociferous fans and several were giving him their most strident opinions.

Anger mostly towards the free kick which led to the goal, but it didn’t seem too egregious a decision to me.

Score is very harsh on Palace, though with Kamada, Strand Larsen and Pino all coming desperately close. Exactly the sort of hard luck story you’d expect from a team in trouble.

We lead at the break 👊 #CRYLIV https://t.co/7e9WF0j1KA.

Despite Szoboszlai’s enforced absence and Liverpool’s numerical disadvantage, Barcola leads an attack that creates a shooting opportunity for Wirtz, which is blocked by Disasi. From the resulting corner, Jacquet nods the ball into Araujo’s path, but he can’t quite sort his feet out and fluffs his lines from close range.

It has been revealed that there will be three minutes of added time at end this first half. There’s a break in play as Szoboszlai is down and in need of treatment.

Industry observers note that alisson produces another sensational stop. A teasing cross is glanced towards goal by Wharton, whose header is parried away by the diving Liverpool goalkeeper. Alisson has been in inspired form so far this afternoon.

Palace almost instantly reply as Mac Allister blocks Timber’s effort, before Alisson tips away the Palace’s midfielder’s long-range shot.

Industry observers note that the visitors have the lead. Szoboszlai whips in a free kick and Mac Allister escapes Timber at the near post, before glancing a brilliant header into the far bottom corner.

Industry observers note that liverpool have taken the lead against Crystal Palace thanks to Alexis Mac Alister's header! 💥 https://t.co/kNal7qsQ35.

Alisson comes to Liverpool’s rescue as Kamada’s meets a cross with a volley, but the goalkeeper produces an incredible reaction to parry the ball away.

In a recent development, barcola finds space at the back post and connects with Szoboszlai’s searching cross thanks to a smashed first-time volley under no pressure, but he hits it over. The winger has to get that on target. That’s a massive chance.

Palace score but the offside flag is up! Liverpool fail to clear a Palace corner as Mingueza finds Pino with a clipped cross. The Spaniard fires the ball across goal and Kamada diverts it into Strand Larsen’s path. From close range, the striker chips into the net and rushes to the corner flag to celebrate. However, his joy is cut short by the offside flag. VAR checks and confirms the onfield decision.

According to recent reports, szoboszlai swivels and tries to find Wirtz with an intricate pass. The German playmaker made a darting run into the penalty area, but Wharton was there to make a pivotal sliding interception.

Jacquet rises highest within a sea of bodies to meet Szoboszlai’s corner, but he loops a header over the bar.

Recent findings suggest that araujo takes a loose touch and lunges into a late challenge on Mitchell, catching the Englishman on the ankle. The Palace bench jump up and the home players rush to the referee, who pulls out a yellow card. Araujo’s tackle was reckless and dangerous. It’s right on the verge of a red, but he escapes that punishment. The Liverpool defender needs to be careful now.

Industry observers note that palace strike the bar! The hosts make a rare foray forward as Mitchell finds Pino with a pinpoint cross. The Spaniard weaves into some space between two Liverpool defenders and slams a powerful half-volley against the woodwork.

Szoboszlai hangs a deep cross towards the back post. Gakpo directs it back across goal with a first-time volley, but no Liverpool has the attacking instinct to take a chance and anticipate it. Isak was instead loitering near the penalty spot. The visitors are well on top here.

Palace have been careless in possession so far, prompting groans from the home support. Szoboszlai draws a save from Henderson with a bobbling long-range strike, forcing the Palace captain into conceding a corner.

Sources indicate that liverpool are popping the ball around with real intent as Gakpo clips a teasing cross into Barcola. It’s just out of the winger’s reach, with Barcola claiming he was pushed by Mingueza. After seeing the replays, the Palace man just eased the Frenchman off the ball. There was minimal contact. Liverpool then win a free kick after Mingueza blocks Kerkez’s run, but Mac Allister glances Szoboszlai’s cross into the side netting at the near post.

Fun start. Palace have occasionally looked like they are hanging on for dear life when defending, especially whenever Gakpo has been on the ball, but have looked capable of some attacking threat of their own, through Pino and Timber especially. Barcola the first example of a player obeying Iraola’s advice to go down more, collapsing from a gentle push after climbing for a header he was never like to reach. Gets short shrift from the referee and Palace fans.

According to recent reports, it’s been a fast-paced and frantic start to this game. Isak’s delightful touch takes him away from Disasi, who pulls the Liverpool forward to the ground, giving the visitors a free kick. The Palace defender is perhaps lucky to avoid a yellow card for that foul.

Mitchell lashes a dangerous delivery across the six-yard box towards Strand Larsen, but solid defensive work from Van Dijk and Araujo allow Liverpool to clear.

It has been revealed that barcola lofts a ball over the top of Palace’s backline for Isak to latch onto. However, Disasi recovers well and blocks the Liverpool striker’s fierce half-volley from a tight angle.

A loose pass at the back from Palace gifts Liverpool an early opportunity, but Henderson does well to get down low and gather Mac Allister’s low, fizzing effort from outside the penalty area.

Liverpool get us under way at Selhurst Park. Can Iraola inflict more misery on Sage?

Industry observers note that this is my second visit to Selhurst since the Holmesdale Fanatics ultras group decided to hang up their large drum and all-black outfits. The atmosphere is noticeably less fierce. A pretty meek rendition of Glad All Over greets the players as they come out of the tunnel, althoiugh it is hardly the sort of rabble-rousing song to strike fear into an opponent at the best of times. Now you will experience the full power of the Dave Clark Five.

The whole of Selhurst Park observes a minute’s silence to remember those who lost their lives in war.

According to recent reports, the Palace and Liverpool players are out on the pitch. Both sides are looking to return to winning ways in the Premier League before the international break.

Andoni Iraola discusses why Liverpool's away form has been much stronger than at home 🗣️ https://t.co/fnuiT3BCLw.

For fans of reading too much into the warm-ups I would say Liverpool already have the edge. Looked like a tight, pacey session for Liverpool, with players practising one-touch passing and closing one another down at pace. More of an old school approach for Palace, some shots at a keeper pretending to dive properly and that classic English football activity - standing as far as you can from one another and hoofing the ball back and forth.

"We know what to expect" 💪 Adam Wharton indicates Crystal Palace are aware of the threats Liverpool pose, but are ready for the clash at Selhurst Park https://t.co/Enhh2hrS2Y.

With an imminent international break around the corner, could Pierre Sage’s time at Palace be up is they suffer another defeat?

2. Dominik Szoboszlai, a man described by my colleague Dom King as “an enigma,” after his performance in the 3-2 defeat against Fenerbahce. “How can a player with the gift of being able to score goals from the heavens make the mistakes of a weekend amateur?”.

On Saturday 27 September 2025, Crystal Palace beat Liverpool 2-1 at Selhurst Park, with Eddie Nketiah striking a 97th-minute winner to send Oliver Glasner’s side second in the Premier League table after six matches. This was Liverpool’s first league defeat of the 2025-26 season as reigning champions under Arne Slot.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Crystal Palace and Liverpool at Selhurst Park.

Selhurst Park 📌 https://t.co/LhCBuWmvMP.

In a recent development, the pressure is building on Palace head coach Pierre Sage, who desperately needs a win to lift the mood and propel the club out of the relegation zone. Nottingham Forest’s impressive 3-1 win over Manchester City on Saturday evening means that Palace have dropped to a lowly 19th and are two points from safety. To make matters worse, Sage’s beleaguered side have also conceded the most goals in the division (21 in nine games).

On Thursday night, Daichi Kamada’s stoppage-time equaliser rescued a 1-1 home draw in the Europa League against Hoffenheim, after Palace delivered an alarmingly lacklustre performance.

Meanwhile, Liverpool also endured midweek European torment, as Andoni Iraola’s men fell to an error-ridden 3-2 defeat away at Fenerbahce in the Champions League, having previously lost 1-0 to Arsenal in their most recent Premier League encounter on Merseyside last weekend, which has left the club in sixth but just five points behind second-place Man City.

Sources indicate that speaking to reporters on Friday, Iraola stated: “I think that’s the challenge, especially in a club like Liverpool. One week ago in this same press conference, we were on a run, everything was in a good place and we were in a better mood. And now, two defeats, it changes. It has to change and it has to be like this in a club like ours. Now we have to react after two defeats.”.

It has been revealed that as for Palace’s team news, Jean-Philippe Mateta is serving the first match of a three-game domestic ban after he was sent off for Palace in the 2-0 defeat to Tottenham last time out in the league. Liverpool’s long-term absentees include Hugo Ekitike, Giovanni Leoni, Conor Bradley and Jeremie Frimpong, while Ryan Gravenberch could also miss out after struggling with a heel injury.

Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news arriving shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Jeremy Doku has revealed he did not think about Manchester City’s Premier League charges when he signed a new five-year contract this summer.

The winger put pen to paper on a five-year deal in August and, the following month, City were found guilty of 114 charges by an independent panel.

While City are appealing against the verdict and are adamant they are innocent, possible punishments could include significant points deductions that result in relegation or ensure they miss out on Champions League football.

But Doku, a 2023 signing from Rennes, remarked it was a simple decision for him to agree to stay at the Etihad Stadium until 2031.

"I don't think it is a difficult thing for me to sign a latest contract,” he explained. “When you look at this club, the trophies they won, it was a easy choice for me. I am happy here, my wife and son are here. It was an easy choice for me. I didn't think a lot, things needed to be right, as soon as everything was from both sides, it was an easy choice.”.

He noted the charges did not come into consideration, adding: "I signed because I was happy to sign, I didn't think about anything else.".

Maresca has referred to City’s off-field troubles as “noise” and Doku is trying to ignore it.

"I know this is all juicy for you guys but we have a massive week, Napoli [on Tuesday] and Arsenal,” he mentioned. “We have enough to speak about. I am not the right person to speak about the charges, I don't really want to get on that topic. I can speak about football.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shares of US artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic saw their first day of trading on Thursday on the US tech-heavy Nasdaq stock exchange.

Anthropic is one of the global leaders in AI technology and is best known for its Claude chatbot.

The stock opened at $111.50 (€101.7) — that's 34% higher than the IPO price of $83 and puts the company's valuation at $2 trillion. Anthropic stock ended the first day of trading at $97 per share.

The company's share performance is being seen as a key test of investor appetite for AI, as stock prices have swung wildly in recent months.

The San Francisco-based organization behind the Claude AI tool has offered 980 million shares at $83 per share, raising a record $81 billion.

This valued the firm at $1.5 trillion, well above market estimates of around $1.3 trillion.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that anthropic is the first big AI firm to go public. Its main competitor, ChatGPT-maker OpenAI,  has reportedly pushed its IPO to 2027.

Issuing shares on the stock market is essentially a way to raise money and avoid taking on debt.

Anthropic has already taken on $6.2 billion in debt and is not yet making a profit. At the same time, it faces massive bills for computer power and data centers.

That specific financial situation is one of the reasons for persistent concern that the AI boom might be a bubble that will eventually burst.

The best European strikers this century - ranked by you

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2095 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Classic number nines, penalty-box poachers, troublesome targetmen and tireless all-rounders.
  • There is no one-size fits all when it comes to determining great strikers, but they do all share a common trait - a ruthlessness in front of goal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The top 10 European strikers of the 21st century.

Classic number nines, penalty-box poachers, troublesome targetmen and tireless all-rounders.

There is no one-size fits all when it comes to determining great strikers, but they do all share a common trait - a ruthlessness in front of goal.

This week, however, we put the power in your hands to decide the best European frontmen of the 21st century.

Tens of thousands of you voted on the 20-man shortlist drawn up by our panel.

We then asked European football experts Guillem Balague, Julien Laurens and Raphael Honigstein to discuss your choices on the Euro Leagues podcast.

So from 10-1, here are the best European strikers this century - as voted for by you.

Top 10 European Strikers of the Century - Part One.

Karim Benzema comes in at number 10, the former Lyon and Real Madrid frontman's closest challengers coming from across the continent in the shape of Raul, Robin van Persie, Michael Owen and Miroslav Klose.

In a recent development, laurens: "From a young age you could see he was something special. I know it was difficult at the beginning at Real Madrid, but in the post-Cristiano era he carried that team, wore the armband and won substantial titles and trophies by being decisive in big moments. Like I used to say 'Karim the dream'.".

Sources indicate that honigstein: "The selflessness, the ability to work for the team. A sense of elegance and humility on the pitch, which is unusual in a goalscorer. I think he is unusual in that list. I think not many will define themselves through their teamwork and assists as much as their goals, but he was that player.".

Ruud van Nistelrooy edges Benzema, with whom he briefly overlapped at Real Madrid - the Dutchman teed up the Frenchman and scored himself in their only La Liga appearance together, before he left for Hamburg in January 2010 following injury problems.

The former PSV striker's most consistent spell, of course, came at Manchester United, where he scored 150 goals.

In a recent development, honigstein: "He is the nicest guy but he never came across that way on the pitch. Typical trait of a striker, he would kill to score the goal. I think anyone who has grown up with him scoring goals, for United especially, must have a soft spot for him because he was a phenomenal poacher.".

Laurens: "He was a strong player physically, and despite the lack of pace the awareness in the box was just very special even with all the injuries.".

Industry observers note that zlatan Ibrahimovic slots in at eight, comfortably clear of Van Nistelrooy and Benzema. The Swede netted more than 500 times in a career that spanned Malmo, Ajax, Juventus, both Milans, Barcelona, Paris St-Germain, Manchester United and LA Galaxy.

Balague: "He was a significant-game player and that explains the league titles with PSG. Scoring four goals against England, the overhead kick. The personality thing has put him one or two places in this list, saying 'I am great, I am the best'. If you keep saying you're great it makes people stop and think.".

It has been revealed that laurens: "The mentality of really believing he was the best and nobody was better than him, apart from maybe Brazilian Ronaldo, who was his idol growing up, and he would watch videos of him and try to replicate in his council estate. If you watch a highlight reel of his best goals he was incredible.".

It has been revealed that honigstein: "What makes him unique among the strikers is his technique, You could see elements of martial arts in his goals. No-one scores goals like that.".

The first Englishman on the list, although the third to have represented Manchester United - it's the Old Trafford outfit's record goalscorer, Wayne Rooney.

It has been revealed that honigstein: "I don't think there is anyone who would've watched English football at that time [early in his career] and not been enthralled by his game. The only downside is the combination of injuries and not the most professional lifestyle meant he did not fulfil his potential. He could've been Messi.".

Balague: "What could have been, yes. He was the national team's record scorer too before Harry Kane took it. I find him to deserve this place as he had to adapt to a lot of strikers and he did it well. He had the ability to link up and score. He was very intelligent.".

In a recent development, laurens: "He is the most street footballer England has ever seen. There's no rules, that kind of anger you saw on the pitch. I don't think people in England realise how good he was.".

Recent findings suggest that what does becoming the all-time World Cup top goalscorer get you? Sixth place on the best European strikers this century list. The Real Madrid forward, 27, just misses out on the top five.

According to recent reports, laurens: "Maybe if we do this ranking again in a few years he will be higher. I would have had him top five, for sure. He has scored more than 400 goals. I don't think Messi and Ronaldo had scored that many at that age, so he's ahead. I don't know if he will play for as long as them but he hasn't done much wrong in his career.".

Balague: "This list has to do what you feel about the player, not science - 22 goals in 22 appearances in World Cups and [Euro] Championships. He should be at least top three because of that. Great stats, but we're not in love with him.".

Honigstein: "I don't think there is a forward that is as good as footballer as him in 2026. On that basis alone he should be higher, but people when they vote have other things in their head. The only way to win everyone over is to score more goals and win more World Cups for France, which I think is possible.".

In a recent development, there was little between Mbappe and Erling Haaland, but it is Manchester City's prolific Norwegian who slips in at fifth. The 26-year-old has already scored more than 300 club goals and has a staggering 68 in 61 games for his country.

Balague: "Mbappe should be higher than him. Haaland scored 52 goals in 53 games [in 2022-23], that is astonishing, but he's gone 11 finals without scoring. We're talking about the best. We're talking about what we see at the moment and what we see is someone who is calculated but in a more charming way. An ability to score we haven't seen in a while; power, ability to finish. He is not world class to the level of others.".

Honigstein: "I don't think it's fair to judge him on just that. They [Manchester City] won the Champions League when he was there. When Haaland arrived with Pep Guardiola, they found a way to do it. What makes him unique is the physical attributes and the pace. To have both is unique. He can sprint like a 100m sprinter. Is he the fifth best striker of the 21st Century? I don't think he's that far behind.".

Interesting, this, because Robert Lewandowski is well clear of Haaland in fourth, but the leap from the Polish forward to the top three is massive - more than 10,000 votes.

The 38-year-old is still chipping away for Chicago Fire in Major League Soccer, having been a reliably ruthless assassin for Barcelona, Bayern and Dortmund.

Industry observers note that honigstein: "He used to play basketball, judo, handball - his father wanted him to have a wholesome education. You could see his completeness that he had as a centre-forward. Nothing in his game was extraordinary but in terms of ticking all the boxes, none come close to him.".

In a recent development, balague: "He said he learned to be an elite striker when he forgot what he had just done, like a fish. Mistakes he had in his head affected his performance. One day he just continued like it didn't matter.".

Laurens: "He won the Ballon d'Or in Covid, it won't be on his mantlepiece but we all know it was his.".

Fresh from his Ballon d'Or triumph, England's record goalscorer and appearance maker rides into the top three on the back of 61 goals in 51 outings for Bayern Munich last season.

Kane left the Premier League three years ago with the second-most goals ever in the competition, and is also Tottenham's all-time record scorer.

Honigstein: "Third place, at least. He is doing incredible things. At 33, still not quite at his peak. I don't think he relies on his pace, physicality, it's all about intelligence, technique. I don't think there's anyone in the game that strikes a ball as well as him right now. I don't think any player comes close that we've talked about so far in overall work-rate, defending, helping the team, making tackles in your box in the 90th minute when you're 3-0 up because he's that kind of guy. He is humble and a superb human being.".

Laurens: "What I love about Kane, from a young age, a lot of this list you just knew the trajectory would be all the way to the top. Kane was not like that. It could have been very different for him. Nobody at 17 would've said he was going to win the Ballon d'Or. Nobody believed in him like the others. Kane had a very different journey.".

Runner-up Thierry Henry is the only striker in the top six who is retired. A World Cup and Euros winner with France, Henry won titles with Arsenal - where he scored 228 goals - and a Champions League with Barcelona.

Honigstein: "During his time, I don't think there was a player like him in the Premier League. The way he played football was stylish, elegant, but there was almost a kind of a romantic connection between him and the ball. I don't think there was anyone near that kind of level of technique and, for want of a better word, va-va-voom he exuded. That just made for amazing viewing.".

Sources indicate that laurens: "For me as a fellow Parisien, he's a very special player, a very special man. A career that has been incredible from a young age. It's that season in the Premier League - 24 goals, 20 assists in 38 games - not even Kane or Benzema or Cristiano, OK, Messi is different, but they haven't done that and yet he did it.

According to recent reports, "There are still some people who undervalue him and underappreciate him and the monster that he was on the football pitch. He had it all. The pace, the style, the elegance, the technique, the mentality, the goals, the aura, the charisma. Just everything you wanted if you were to build a striker. One of the greatest football brains ever.".

In a recent development, of course, at number one, it's the man chasing the 1,000-goal dream. Cristiano Ronaldo may have retired from Portugal duty with 146 notches on his strike chart but the quest goes on at Al-Nassr.

The 41-year-old's evolution from tricky winger to prolific frontman has taken him from Sporting to Manchester United, twice, Real Madrid, Juventus and now Saudi Arabia.

In a recent development, balague: "He's the best striker in history. His numbers are incredible. He won't stop until he gets to 1,000. He is somebody who is special. We know his background, how he wanted to be Ballon d'Or winner at 12 and didn't stop until he got there. He ran up the mountains of Funchal with weights in his ankles and snuck into the gym when it was closed to get the physique he wanted.".

Laurens: "Always in the right place at the right time. The instinct. He was born with a gift, like all in this list. But you still have to work hard. Nobody will ever reach those levels again. 1,000 goals for club and country will never be done again, I think.".

Sources indicate that honigstein: "Peak Ronaldo for me was Gareth Bale scoring and him looking very unhappy. I don't think there will be any dispute about him being the greatest. Somebody who has done it all, won it all, and he's still going for the love of it.".

#162634. How Man United fans revolted against the Glazers to create their own football club

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 15m • 📚 Deep Dive (3061 w)

How Man United fans revolted against the Glazers to create their own football club

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (3061 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fourfourtwo

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, revolution can spark in the most unlikely places.
  • Fully 36 years after that legendary ‘bed-in’, a group of football supporters chose an equally unlikely venue to kick-start their own revolution.
  • It has been revealed that “There was a buzz in the air,” explains Jules Spencer, a lifelong Manchester United fan who attended the event and had taken part in other protests.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, revolution can spark in the most unlikely places. John Lennon knew that. The former Beatle and wife Yoko Ono needed only an Amsterdam hotel room to stage their 1969 protest over the Vietnam War. Lennon’s decision to start a revolution from his bed would later be immortalised in the lyrics of Oasis’ Imagine pastiche Don’t Look Back in Anger.

Fully 36 years after that legendary ‘bed-in’, a group of football supporters chose an equally unlikely venue to kick-start their own revolution. Outraged by a hostile takeover of their beloved Manchester United, and fed up with where football appeared to be heading in general, they convened in May 2005 to discuss a notion that would send shockwaves through the English game. The meeting place: Methodist Central Hall in Manchester’s Northern Quarter.

It has been revealed that “There was a buzz in the air,” explains Jules Spencer, a lifelong Manchester United fan who attended the event and had taken part in other protests. “We’d fought against change before, including Rupert Murdoch’s attempted takeover. But this was the final straw.”.

Back in 1999, the United Kingdom’s Competition Commission had blocked Murdoch and BSkyB’s £625 million bid for Manchester United, the government’s reasoning that the acquisition would have “hurt competition in the broadcast industry and the quality of British football”. The next major power grab would not be so easily thwarted, though.

In a recent development, malcolm Glazer, an American business tycoon and owner of NFL franchise the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, had first bought nearly three per cent of Manchester United in March 2003. Through a series of incremental buyouts, that stake neared 30 per cent by October 2004 – a threshold above which Glazer would have to launch a formal takeover bid.

Businessmen muscling into football was nothing latest, but as the takeover drew nearer supporters became increasingly concerned. Most of the capital used by Glazer to buy the club would come in the form of loans, the majority of which were secured against the club’s assets, incurring average interest payments of more than £46m per annum.

“It was,” lifelong Red Devils fan Paul Hurst notes, “absolutely scandalous.”.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

It has been revealed that in February 2005, hundreds of United fans protested outside Old Trafford, with some hanging an effigy of Glazer. That month, the idea for a breakaway club was first mooted by now defunct fanzine Red Issue.

Recent findings suggest that “As the spectre of Malcolm Glazer looms ever larger, the question has been increasingly asked: ‘What would you do if he did take over?’” they penned. “What if you could give up supporting Glazer’s firm without giving up United?

“Back in the days of the Murdoch campaign, an evacuation plan was drawn up, detailing the blueprint for the formation of a newly introduced Manchester United, one which spurned the commercialism and tackiness of the modern game, and was controlled and run by the fans. With United again under threat, those prepares have been resurrected. With a working name of ‘FC United’, the logistics of the operation to set up a new Manchester United has been looked into.”.

The article outlined the bold ambition. “We would await regime change, while aiding all attempts to undermine the illegitimate occupation,” it continued. “When Glazer is defeated, FC United will be happy to return to Old Trafford and merge with ‘the franchise’ on condition that the supporters’ trust maintains full ownership of the football club and the unified Manchester United take over the higher league position of FC United. Viva la revolucion.”.

Three months later, Glazer completed his takeover, reaching the 75 per cent threshold required to end the club’s public limited organization (PLC) status and delist from the London Stock Exchange.

It prompted fans to assemble and discuss a fresh club at Methodist Central Hall, complete with Styrofoam cups of tea in hand, surrounded by murals of Bible scenes and psalms.

“I’d taken part in the protests against the Glazers, along with so many others,” says Hurst, who was at that meeting. “Many of us pledged not to give the club one penny more while Glazer owned it. We wouldn’t be paying off his debts.”.

Sources indicate that “It wasn’t about switching off our allegiance to Manchester United – that would never go,” remembers Spencer. “It was about letting Manchester United and the Glazers know that we wouldn’t stand idly by and allow this to happen. If necessary, we were willing to put our money towards something else instead, something positive to be proud of.”.

Red Issue editor John-Paul O’Neill organised the new movement, backed by a steering committee. “It was drawn from across the fanbase, from official fan groups to business people and those with marketing and communications expertise,” says team member Spencer. “We held more meetings, with around 1,500 people joining at Manchester’s Apollo theatre. Not everybody was convinced, but they came along to hear what we had to say. Momentum began to build and some fans started to pledge their United season ticket money to help us get off the ground. It was so exciting.”.

Industry observers note that preparations included a visit from Kris Stewart, chairman of AFC Wimbledon, founded three years earlier. “His insight was invaluable,” recalls Spencer. “We didn’t really know what we were doing at that stage. He told us we were in for a lot of hard work and that a lot would go wrong, but it’d be totally worth it if we pulled it off. He remained a valued sounding board in the months to come.”.

Industry observers note that time was of the essence. The new club had to be set up and registered well before the new 2005-06 season, already less than two months away. Failing to do so would risk losing momentum. They didn’t even have a name.

The FA vetoed ‘FC United’ for being too generic, so those who’d pledged money were asked to vote on a different name. Manchester Central and Newton Heath United were discarded as options – in June, ‘FC United of Manchester’ got the nod and joined the 10th-tier North West Counties Division Two. While it wasn’t their official moniker, many called them FC United anyway.

In a recent development, there was still the not insignificant matter of finding some players. Some 900 applications were whittled down to 200 trialists, from which Karl Marginson, the club’s inaugural manager, would select a squad of 17.

“The standard of the trialists was very strong and we put together a team I felt capable of challenging for the title in our first campaign,” he tells FFT now.

How did the manager get the gig? “It was between me and one other bloke, and he was a Scouser,” Marginson, a born-and-bred Manc chuckles. “I was 34 – I’d been an assistant at Flixton, so not had a proper manager’s job before, but I knew the league well.

According to recent reports, “I’d been a Manchester United fan all my life and didn’t like where the original club was heading. I didn’t think my own kids would be able to afford to go when they were old enough, the way I had as a teenager, and that was so wrong. The new club was notable and I think they could see what it meant to me as well. I was young and ambitious – the idea of taking charge of a totally new club appealed to me.”.

Their first match was a drab 0-0 draw at Leigh RMI. The pre-season friendly was watched by more than 2,500 fans, TV crews and national journalists. “It was magnificent and bonkers at the same time,” claims Marginson. “There was a party atmosphere in the air, even for such a terrible game. I couldn’t believe what I’d let myself in for.”.

A similar-sized crowd flocked to FC United’s first competitive match, a 5-2 victory at Leek County School Old Boys, whose ground was used to hosting fans by the dozen, not the thousand. Home matches, staged at Bury’s Gigg Lane as part of a long-term groundsharing deal, delivered gates as large as 6,000 during a season that consistently smashed the league’s attendance records.

Recent findings suggest that “It was incredible to see,” reminisces future board member Hurst. “The level of football was very different to what we’d been used to, nine divisions higher in the Premier League, but the sense of community more than made up for it.”.

In a recent development, the matchday mood wasn’t always positive, though. Throughout the club’s formation, a small yet vocal group of Manchester United supporters had railed against the movement, branding those involved traitors. Tensions flared during a game against Salford City. “The fixture had to be switched to Salford’s rugby league ground due to the expected crowd,” explains Hurst.

“Lots of Manchester United fans bought tickets to protest against us, which was ironic. They had some banners calling us turncoats and all the rest of it. It got quite unpleasant.”.

Even Sir Alex Ferguson weighed in on the upcoming club, labelling the movement “a shame” and questioning whether those involved were really proper Red Devils to begin with.

According to recent reports, “Listen, we could all understand the criticism to a certain degree,” continues Hurst. “The new club was divisive, even within families and friendship circles.

Recent findings suggest that “There were those that saw it as the genuine protest movement it was – a necessary act of defiance – and others who saw us as Judases who turned our back on the club in its hour of need. That was never the case.

“Many of us are passionate Manchester United supporters. We just didn’t want to fund Glazer’s debts by going to games. Thankfully, a lot of that hatred has died down since.”.

On-field headlines were positive. The Red Rebels swept to the Division Two title in their first season, finishing eight points clear of Marginson’s former club Flixton. “A fantastic achievement,” he says. “It was vital to show that we were a club that meant business in footballing terms as well, beyond the protest club element.”.

In a recent development, they were far from done. FC United won promotion again in their second campaign, then another in their third to reach the Northern Premier Division, two levels below the National League and three from the EFL.

A fourth promotion was squandered in 2010-11, courtesy of a play-off final defeat to Colwyn Bay. Earlier in that season, FC United had advanced to the FA Cup first round for the first time, then won at League One Rochdale to set up a second round showdown at Brighton, who would go on to win the third tier that term.

Recent findings suggest that the 10-man Red Rebels even led at the Withdean Stadium, before Mauricio Taricco’s late equaliser earned Gus Poyet’s Seagulls a replay they would win 4-0 at Gigg Lane. The 6,900 gate that night was more than 1,500 higher than the first encounter in East Sussex.

It has been revealed that further play-off defeats followed in 2012, 2013 and 2014. “I definitely felt the pressure to win matches and keep taking the football club forward,” says Marginson. “I was still inexperienced and we were getting huge attendances to every game.

“We had one of the bigger budgets in those leagues and supporters expected a lot. I already drank alcohol, but I’d be lying if I stated I didn’t lean into that a bit more to help cope.”.

Promotion eventually came in 2015 – not only did FC United secure a fifth successive top-six finish, this time they won the league, during a campaign in which they groundshared with Curzon Ashton and Stalybridge Celtic. “It was an epic achievement,” claims Marginson with pride. “The club stuck by me and we got there in the end.”.

The timing couldn’t have been better, with a newly introduced 4,700-capacity home all of their own ready to move into.

“Gigg Lane served us incredibly well, but financially it made more sense for us to have somewhere permanent,” notes director Hurst. “We scouted out a number of sites before the council let us build a fresh stadium in Moston.”.

Located just four miles north-east of Manchester city centre, Broadhurst Park cost £6.5m and hosted its first match, a friendly against Benfica B, on May 29 that year – the same date on which Manchester United beat Benfica in the 1968 European Cup Final. “It felt like a massive step for us,” adds Spencer. “A place to stand with our friends, our sons and daughters, and call home.”.

FC United finished a respectable 13th in the National League North on two occasions, but a tough start to 2017-18 resulted in Marginson’s exit. “If you’d have told me when I first took the job that I’d still have been there all those years later, I’d have remarked, ‘No chance’,” he says, reflecting on 12 years in charge. “I think back to the young man I was when I became manager – it’s a world apart. I couldn’t have done the job had I been older. It needed youth and energy from the off. Eventually, I ran out.”.

In a recent development, A newly introduced injection arrived in the form of striker Tom Greaves – the club’s all-time top scorer – who stepped up to a player-manager role. He steered the club to survival but departed after a poor start to the next campaign, to be replaced by Neil Reynolds. He, though, couldn’t turn the tide, with FC United relegated back to the Northern Premier Division. COVID annulled 2019-20 when they were sat second and set for the play-offs again – five years on, they’re yet to return to the sixth tier of the pyramid.

Sources indicate that not that it’s all been doom and gloom. Later in 2020, FC United reached the FA Cup first round for the third time, facing League One Doncaster Rovers in front of the live TV cameras. A year after that, they were invited to participate in the inaugural Fenix Trophy, a tournament contested by a selection of unusual non-league sides from across Europe. The Mancunians travelled to face AKS Zly in Warsaw, and Brera in Milan, going on to beat Prague Raptors in the final in the Italian city of Rimini.

Sources indicate that in 2022-23, they again reached the latter stages of the competition, losing a semi to BK Skjold of Denmark but then beating Brera at Milan’s San Siro, no less. Last season, after matches in Krakow and Paris, they won the cup for a second time, defeating Prague Raptors in the final once more, on the shores of Lake Garda on this occasion.

“I certainly didn’t envisage leading my team-mates out at San Siro when I first joined,” says club captain Charlie Ennis, who arrived in the summer of 2019. “Getting changed in Milan’s dressing room and walking out onto that iconic pitch – it still gives me goosebumps now. We’ve been very lucky to be a part of the competition, travelling across Europe. It’s been one of the highlights of my career.”.

According to recent reports, ennis, now 34, is another who didn’t expect to stay as long as he has. “I was no spring chicken when I signed,” he jokes. “But I’m a local lad and, short of playing for Manchester United, who I grew up supporting, there’s nowhere else I’d rather be. We get big crowds, play at a fantastic ground and this club means so much to people. The best years are yet to come.”.

The man tasked with leading them into the next era is gaffer Mark Beesley, who replaced Reynolds in September after resigning from Warrington Town. His squad includes 38-year-old former Reading and Bolton forward Adam Le Fondre, a lifelong Manchester United fan who spoke of semi-fulfilling a dream when signing from Scottish Premiership side Hibernian last summer.

Whatever the future holds, FC United can already look back on the past two decades with enormous pride. “It’s been a lot of hard work, but I wouldn’t have changed it for the world,” director Hurst tells FFT now. “You look over at Manchester United, what continues to happen at the club with its ownership, and you’d be hard pressed to say we were wrong to do this. We’ve given local football fans a positive alternative.”.

Industry observers note that manchester United are still majority-owned by the Glazers. Malcolm passed the reins to his sons before his death in 2014. Since the family took charge, it’s estimated the club has paid out more than £750m in interest fees on loan repayments alone. Debts remain high, while on-field success has steadily declined since Ferguson’s retirement. Ineos impresario Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s £1bn investment for a 27.7 per cent stake has rekindled neither success nor spirit.

Recent findings suggest that “We want more than anything for that to change, for the Glazers to sell up, and for Manchester United to become a well-run club again,” indicates Spencer. “I’m still a Manchester United fan. I was jumping for joy when we beat City in last season’s FA Cup final. But as long as the Glazers are still there, I can’t be.”.

According to recent reports, until that day, and long after, Spencer and his fellow rebels will be found at Broadhurst Park. “I come here with my sons and it’s a special feeling,” he notes. “It’s something positive that we can all share as a community. I look back at that meeting at the church hall all those years ago and can’t help but laugh at how far we’ve come since. We made the right decision.

Ed is a staff writer at FourFourTwo, working across the magazine and website. A German speaker, he’s been working as a football reporter in Berlin since 2015, predominantly covering the Bundesliga and Germany's national team. Favourite FFT features include an exclusive interview with Jude Bellingham following the youngster’s move to Borussia Dortmund in 2020, a history of the Berlin Derby since the fall of the Wall and a celebration of Kevin Keegan’s playing career.

#162633. Welcome to Man United, Mauricio Pochettino. It’s awful

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (957 w)

Welcome to Man United, Mauricio Pochettino. It’s awful

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (957 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later?
  • Recent findings suggest that welcome to Manchester United, Mauricio.
  • It has been revealed that “So painful,” Pochettino remarked.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Recent findings suggest that welcome to Manchester United, Mauricio. For a man who had coveted the United job for years, this was an ignominious introduction. Mauricio Pochettino got a 13-minute crash course in the craziness of his upcoming club. His first game was lost before he made his first substitution, and that came as early as the 22nd-minute. His debut brought the joint heaviest ever defeat by a United manager in his first game in charge, and the biggest in 100 years.

It has been revealed that “So painful,” Pochettino remarked. “So disappointed.” As can be the way with United of late, most things that could go wrong did. When their new head coach’s name was sung, it was by the Kop. “Poch is at the wheel,” they taunted. A first meaningful day of work demonstrated the scale of the task to steer United in the right direction.

The team who exhibited the pace and energy of the best Pochettino sides were Liverpool, relishing the chance to compound their rivals’ problems. Florian Wirtz scored a glorious goal, Bradley Barcola kept demonstrating a sprinter’s speed and Rio Ngumoha illuminated Anfield with his precocity. Yet each was aided by United, hapless and hopeless, showing it is easier to change the manager than to reverse one of the most extraordinary declines in English football history.

Sources indicate that it was as though Pochettino’s charges had decided to show him a snapshot of the problems: their self-destructive streak, their defensive failings, their capacity to concede in quick succession. No previous Premier League manager had seen his side both let in two goals and go down to 10 men in the first half of his opening game. Pochettino’s United accomplished that in a quarter of an hour. Suffice to say there was no honeymoon period.

Recent findings suggest that the watching Sir Alex Ferguson had lost his first game in charge, 2-0 at Oxford 40 years ago. Pochettino topped that, in the wrong way. Only Lal Hilditch, in 1926, had begun his reign as badly, with another 4-0 loss.

According to recent reports, and yet there was a continuity to United’s calamity. Meet the new boss, same as the old boss? Despite regime change, some of this was very familiar. United were two goals behind after 18 minutes against Roma, after four against Villa, after 13 against Liverpool. United got rid of Michael Carrick, kept the masterplan of going 2-0 down and discovered it has certain flaws.

It has been revealed that this was scarcely an unlucky 13 for United. Rather, they were culpable in their own downfall. Matthijs de Ligt needlessly left Ronald Araujo’s long ball, Alexander Isak ran behind the United defence and Leny Yoro barged him over. “It was an unfair situation,” complained Pochettino. “It was clear that was not a red card.” Iraola disagreed. “It is clearly the last man, clearly a foul,” he remarked.

So Yoro was sent off by referee Sam Barrott and waved off by the Liverpool faithful. The punishment for United was doubled when Dominik Szoboszlai drilled his free kick past a ramshackle wall and in. Chants of “going down” rang around Anfield. It was replaced, a few minutes later, by “sacked in the morning”.

Recent findings suggest that with wonderful improvisation, Wirtz hooked in a volley after Ngumoha sped past Diogo Dalot and dinked in a cross. If a criticism was that the £100m German had influenced too few major matches in his Liverpool career, he altered this, brilliantly, and ended with an assist to accompany his second goal in as many games. “He's in a lovely moment,” mentioned Iraola.

Liverpool slowed down at the end of the first half and then sped up again after the break. Barcola’s profligate finishing had cost him Liverpool’s third goal but his extraordinary pace created it. The £106m man’s scorched-earth solo run was followed by a pass to allow Ngumoha to replace Michael Owen as Liverpool’s youngest ever scorer against United. The teenager had tormented Dalot, but he was not the only winger on the scoresheet.

Industry observers note that victor Munoz exchanged passes with Wirtz and curled in the fourth after Liverpool’s high pressing was shown as Virgil van Dijk robbed Joshua Zirkzee, 25 yards from the United goal. Iraola ended doing fist pumps to the Kop, Jurgen Klopp-style.

“We probably should have scored more than four,” Iraola said. Senne Lammens saved, from Isak, Alexis Mac Allister and Szoboszlai. Harry Maguire made a brilliant block to turn an Isak shot away. The Swede slashed a shot wide after De Ligt inexplicably missed the ball for a second time.

It reflected badly on the new manager. Perhaps Pochettino’s first significant call was to bring in De Ligt for a first league appearance of 2026. That backfired. Meanwhile, Maguire was first dropped and then summoned.

Pochettino had to keep changing tack. As Liverpool scored four goals, United used four formations. Pochettino seemed to begin by borrowing Ruben Amorim’s 3-4-3, then it looked a 4-2-3-1. Then it was neither, with United down to 10 men. “After what happened, happened and the strategy was in the bin,” remarked Pochettino, who went to first 4-4-1 then 5-3-1, and who tried to argue what he felt was an injustice of a red card rendered what followed rather irrelevant. “We concede four goals with 10 men, and in a circumstance after playing 80 minutes at Anfield,” he said. But the circumstances are that United are in the relegation zone, lost on Pochettino’s bow, and were walloped by their rivals.
