Thomas Tuchel will speak openly to England’s players about what they should do if they encounter racism in the Nations League Group 3 decider with Spain.

Recent findings suggest that this is the first time England have faced Spain in Madrid since November 2004 when they were beaten 1-0 in the Santiago Bernabéu, a game that was ravaged by obscene chanting. The nations were supposed to play a fixture in the Spanish capital in 2008, but the Football Association insisted it be moved to Seville instead.

Earlier this year, Spanish supporters brought shame on themselves again after a flurry of anti-Muslim chants marred a friendly against Egypt; they were fined $20,000 by Fifa and must play their next friendly in a partially closed stadium.

There will be a full house in the Wanda Metropolitano on Sunday night, as the reigning world and European champions aim to defend their extraordinary unbeaten run of 43 games, and England head coach Tuchel is adamant the atmosphere will be in keeping with the occasion.

The German has, however, made it clear he and his staff will use their platform before the contest to remind England’s players of the steps they should take if the worst scenario unfolds.

Asked about incidents that had pockmarked this fixture before, Tuchel stated: “I think I hear it the first time that this happens. I think it’s unacceptable. In any stadium, not even in stadiums, we will never accept racism. We will never be racist towards anyone.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of England’s final Nations League Group 3 decider as Thomas Tuchel’s side take on Spain at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid.

It has been revealed that although both countries are safely through to the quarter-finals, England will seek revenge on Spain, who beat them in the Euro 2024 final and in their previous Nations League face-off on September 26 at Wembley. That day, Luis de la Fuente’s men profited from Harry Kane’s uncharacteristic penalty miss, England’s general wastefulness in front of goal and some seriously lacklustre defending to earn a chaotic 3-2 comeback victory after falling 2-1 behind at half-time.

Since that defeat, England have won four successive Nations League fixtures against the Czech Republic and Croatia by an aggregate score of 14-1. Last time out, they beat Croatia on Thursday, earning a 2-1 win as Kane, who became England’s most-capped men’s player with 126 appearances, dispatched a second-half penalty to seal the three points. Spearheaded by the Ballon d’Or holder’s brilliance, England must win this evening in order to overtake Spain and top the group.

And then you can never predict the result in football, never. But it’s important that we show the mindset that you speak of and the spirit, and we will. I’m very confident about that.”.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, fresh from lifting the World Cup in the summer, Spain have a 100% winning record in this season’s Nations League. They right now boast a staggering 43-match unbeaten run in all competitions, since losing a friendly to Colombia back in March 2024. England’s task is daunting, but not impossible.

Kick-off is at 19:45, with team news coming shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany's flagship airline Lufthansa prepares to cut 1,000 jobs at its Frankfurt and Munich hubs, according to a company letter seen by German news agency DPA and news outlets.

The letter was reportedly signed by Lufthansa CEO Jens Ritter and four other board members.

Sources indicate that this is reportedly down to ongoing financial losses. In the first nine months of the year, the airline recorded an operating loss of €180 million ($197 million).

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that the executive board said on average the loss amounts to €20 million every month, according to media reports. The board stated in the letter that "this is the third year in a row of not being financially successful.".

"Lufthansa is currently not competitive in terms of its cost structure, efficiency and productivity," the letter noted.

At the end of 2025, the Lufthansa group employed some 67,100 people, up 1% from the previous year.

The company also aims to cut employee travel benefits, restructure its hub operations to reduce crew overnight stays abroad, and reduce short- and medium-haul capacity by replacing some A320 aircraft with A220 jets.

Furthermore, it looks to equip ten aircraft per month with Starlink, a satellite internet service developed by tech billionaire Elon Musk. The airline hopes to generate "additional revenue” by monetizing onboard internet access, according to the letter.

It has been revealed that the time frame of the cuts is unclear. It's also unknown whether the cuts were a part of a previously unveiled downsizing.

In September 2025, Lufthansa said it would slash 4,000 administrative positions due to the implementation of AI and digitalization.

In regards to this year, Lufthansa has faced rising fuel costs spurred by the US-Israeli war with Iran, further complicating its financial outlook.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We probably don't need to recap the story, do we? But just in case...

It was 30 years ago exactly, back on 23 November, 1996, when Ali Dia made perhaps the most notorious appearance in the history of Premier League football.

Dia had purported to be the cousin of George Weah to get himself a trial at Graeme Souness' Southampton, and incredibly ended up coming on in place of the injured Matt Le Tissier, only to later be subbed back off hauled back off in the 85th minute of a 2-0 defeat to Leeds.

Dia looked like he'd struggle to play in a Sunday league team, never mind a top-flight outfit - but as Souness explained to FourFourTwo: "That was portrayed like we'd been conned, but no-one was conned.

"Someone phoned up pretending to be George Weah, but we were getting players in every month to come on trial, because we had no money – that's where we got Eyal Berkovic." (Wonder who Berkovic's agent pretended to be?).

"When we got the call about Dia, I remarked, 'Get him in'.

"Within the first five minutes of a small-sided game at training, I realised he wasn't good enough for us.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

"But we didn't have enough players for training sessions, so we said, 'We'll keep him until the end of the week, then we'll tell him'.

"That week we got more and more injuries, to the point where my coach Terry Cooper said, 'We're going to have to have that clown on the bench'.

Recent findings suggest that "I said, 'We can't'. He said, 'We haven't got any players'.

"He was on the bench against Leeds, then Matt Le Tissier comes off injured and I've got a choice between a centre-half, a full-back or a defensive midfielder [or Dia].

"I mentioned, 'Stick Dia on, he'll run about, hopefully occupy their back four'.

"He did that, but he was out of his depth.".

Steven Pressley revealed the embarrassment of Dundee’s 8-0 hammering by Hearts on Saturday left him wanting to “crawl under a rock and hide”.

The Dark Blues manager has shouldered full responsibility after his team suffered their heaviest-ever home league defeat.

In a recent development, speaking as Dundee prepared to return to action at Hibernian on Tuesday, Pressley noted: “It’s been a difficult 24-48 hours. There’s been a lot of hurt, a lot of embarrassment. As you can imagine, at times I’ve wanted to crawl under a rock and hide.

“It’s difficult on the back of such a disappointing result. But I will say this, I suffer a lot from vulnerability at times, but for some reason during difficult moments I seem to find strength from somewhere.

“I don’t know if it’s from my family, from messages that I’ve received, from my reading.

“But I’ve had to show strength, I have to support the players. I have to make sure we navigate our way out of what was a really embarrassing moment.

Recent findings suggest that “We had a good meeting yesterday. We chatted a lot about the various aspects, and hopefully we can start responding to the disappointment.”.

Pressley said he had feared a setback coming for Dundee – “not 8-0 but a disappointing performance” – because he had “sensed a little bit of subconscious complacency”.

The manager felt his team had been over-hyped by outsiders on the back of a start to the season in which they won five of their 12 matches before the international break.

Industry observers note that “We’re nowhere near the levels that people keep telling us we are,” he stressed. “We’re not a good enough team not to do the hard yards. Our whole strength has been built on the cohesion of the team, the unity of the team, the aggressiveness of the team.

“And I think what Saturday did highlight is exactly what I’ve been saying. If we get lazy on the hard yards, we’re a very vulnerable team.

Sources indicate that “We have to be at our absolute best to get results. If we fall below that, we’re nowhere near the levels that people have been telling us we’re at.”.

Recent findings suggest that pressley said Saturday has to represent “a reset moment, a moment we can always come back to to help us become better”. Asked if he expected a positive response from his players at Easter Road just 72 hours on from their Hearts humbling, he said: “I don’t know.

Industry observers note that “I know that they’re hurting. I know that they want to respond in the best possible way. That part I don’t question. I know how much it’s affected them.

Recent findings suggest that “But we’ve not had a lot of time. I just hope we can bring some pride back to the football club with the right type of performance.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you're looking for jeopardy at the top of the Premier League this season, you're looking in the wrong place.

Arsenal, already reigning champions, have so far turned their title defence into an autumn stroll, swatting aside challengers with efficiency, threatening to wrap up another crown at a canter before winter is even through.

Industry observers note that for genuine drama and unpredictability in 2026/27, the centre of gravity in European football has shifted south. Serie A, once a league renowned for miserly defences and low-scoring contests, is serving up the most compelling, wide-open title race on the continent.

If any proof was needed that Italian football has buried its old catenaccio stereotype for good, Sunday evening's 4-4 draw between Atalanta and Inter Milan delivered it.

Far from being a cagey affair, it was pure mayhem with two heavyweights trading blows right up until the final whistle.

That eight-goal epic was no anomaly, either because across Europe’s top five leagues this campaign, Serie A actually leads the way for entertainment in front of goal, averaging 3.08 goals per match.

The Italian top flight is comfortably ahead of the Bundesliga (2.94), the Premier League (2.81), Ligue 1 (2.72) and La Liga (2.56). So, forget 1-0 defensive masterclasses, modern calcio is all about goals.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

According to recent reports, better still, the table looks like a throwback to the division’s 1990s golden era. Only a handful of points separates the leading pack, with several of Italy’s biggest and best-supported institutions - from Milan and Naples to Turin and the capital - are engaged in a multi-club scrap for the Scudetto.

Industry observers note that A key reason for that is the capital roaring back to life. Both Roma and Lazio remain unbeaten 12 games into the season, having spent too many recent campaigns watching their northern rivals monopolise domestic success. The Eternal City’s old powers are title contenders once again, playing with renewed swagger.

The beauty of this Serie A season lies just as much in its new blood as its established giants, becaause perched on the periphery of the title race are Como, one of European football’s coolest and most compelling stories.

Recent findings suggest that their lakeside glamour is neatly juxtaposed by a smart, progressive sporting project and exciting football. They are doing their best to crash the elite party without a hint of an inferiority complex.

Recent findings suggest that for nearly a decade, Juventus’ run of nine consecutive titles drained the suspense from Italian football. Serie A has since become one of Europe’s most competitive major leagues, albeit without continental success. Over the past five years, three different clubs - Inter, AC Milan and Napoli - have lifted the trophy, and not once has it returned to Turin, nor does it look as though that'll be the case this season, either.

Of course, the Premier League still boasts the deepest pockets and the best marketing machine, but when the title race is effectively over before December, spectacle suffers. In Italy, the potential for plot twists retains the intrigue and drama.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spurs secure famous win as Man City falter again.

Dreams of reaching the Women's Champions League may have seemed fanciful for Tottenham Hotspur when the season began.

The Women's Super League has an established massive four, and big-spending London City Lionesses were the side making the most obvious play to disrupt that dominance.

But a hugely impressive and deserved win at Manchester City on Sunday afternoon proves Spurs are a team on the up, and the table shows they remain firmly in top-three contention.

According to recent reports, two late goals secured a 3-1 win at Joie Stadium, but this was no smash-and-grab job. Spurs were more dynamic than sluggish City, pressing them into submission.

They restricted their hosts' stellar attack to precious few chances and took the ones they created.

"When we are on our game, we can be a match for anyone," Spurs manager Martin Ho noted in his post-match media conference.

"It gives us confidence - but it is just one game.".

Man City beaten by Spurs and miss chance to go top of WSL.

Victory kept Spurs, whose highest finish in the WSL is fifth, firmly in the mix this time.

They are fifth again, but just three points behind London City Lionesses who occupy the final European place as the league heads into a last international break of 2026.

Chelsea lead the way from Manchester City, with Manchester United one point ahead of Tottenham, who in turn sit handily clear of their sixth-placed north London rivals Arsenal.

Recent findings suggest that the big four are therefore all present in the top six. London City are right there, too, and Spurs, with six wins from 11 games so far, are gamely pressing their own case.

What made Sunday's win and performance from Tottenham even more impressive is how dreadful their recent record against Manchester City had been.

Tottenham had lost six of their previous seven away matches against City in all competitions, averaging over four goals conceded per defeat.

Last season City won this fixture 5-2 with Khadija Shaw scoring a 13-minute hat-trick, the quickest in WSL history.

Shaw's early goal on Sunday, her 16th in league matches versus Spurs, could easily have started a landslide.

It has been revealed that that was expected. City had won each of their past 17 WSL home games, including all 10 in 2026 â until Tottenham tore up the script.

The outcome means Manchester City, beaten at Chelsea in their previous outing, have suffered consecutive league losses for the first time since January 2025.

Spurs have rediscovered form after losing all three league games in October while conceding 14 goals.

Tottenham's victory came down to Ho's brave tactics and his team's superb execution of them.

After going behind, they pressed City constantly, forcing errors and creating chances. That tenacity won them countless one-on-ones, with City unable or unwilling to play over the press.

After her goal, Shaw was rendered anonymous by the hard work and close marking of centre-backs Toko Koga and Amanda Nilden.

Down the right, Kirsty Hanson dominated Carlotta Wamser, could have been awarded a penalty and provided the low cross for Cathinka Tandberg's equaliser.

It has been revealed that in midfield, Drew Spence pulled all the strings and covered the entire pitch. At 34, she is perhaps playing the best football of her career and deserved her assist for the winner. After Matilda Vinberg put Spurs in front, several players ran to celebrate with Spence.

"When you come into this, you wonder if it will go against you, but the players were outstanding," stated Ho.

Industry observers note that "We haven't won here in so long, so we know it will be a tough game, but I have belief in my team when we are on song. I thought we were outstanding - we worked every blade of grass.".

Spurs are clearly capable of taking the game to anyone in the league and have now scored 28 WSL goals this season, with only Chelsea and London City having more.

In the second half they adapted to City sending on such fluid attacking threats as Mary Fowler, Kerstin Casperij and Beth Mead.

They lifted the gas from the press, applying it more sparingly, and were solid in defence.

It shows that Ho has learned painful lessons from the past - whether from Spurs' poor record against City, including two five-goal losses in 2025-26, or conceding six to Chelsea and London City back to back in October.

"We have maybe been naive at times and I own that, so we are more reserved," Ho said of his tactical approach. "It was managing that, and the players' communication was excellent.".

City were limited to fleeting chances. Jade Rose blasting over after keeper Lize Kop parried a Lauren Hemp free-kick was as close as they came to a second goal, and those were their first shots after a 50-minute drought.

When Spurs got their late chances through the hard work of Vinberg, they could strike for three points.

In a recent development, vinberg had quite the rollercoaster afternoon. She was initially named on the bench but was promoted to the starting XI 15 minutes before kick-off as Olivia Holdt was suffering stomach cramps.

Perhaps unprepared, she gave away the ball playing out of defence leading to City's opener. But she grew into the game, scored Spurs' second goal and set up Jess Naz for the third.

It was a great moment for Naz, on her 100th WSL appearance of a career that has been disrupted by injury.

Spurs are back in Manchester before Christmas, visiting United on 20 December.

There will be real hope of a positive result as they press their way into contention for what would be a historic achievement of a top-three finish.

Man City beaten by Spurs and miss chance to go top of WSL.

Aston Villa were expecting some teething problems in 2026/27, but not being able to rely on home wins keeping them on track probably wasn’t one of them.

According to recent reports, villa seldom looked capable of breaking the deadlock in Saturday’s goalless draw with Sunderland. Their 2-1 win over Manchester City was their only home win in the Premier League in six attempts this season.

Sources indicate that it’s a far cry from the general shape of Villa’s home from since Unai Emery took over as manager in the autumn of 2022. Villa Park has been the bedrock of the Emery revolution, but it’s anything but impenetrable so far this term.

Last season ended in triumph both in the fight for Champions League places and in the Europa League, but Villa’s faltering home form dates back to the start of 2026.

They won their first home match after the turn of the year but they lost their first home match for nearly four months when Everton visited Birmingham and won 1-0 in the middle of January. It was the same result against Brentford in the next home fixture and the aura, suddenly, was weakened.

A spate of midfield injuries affected those matches but Villa’s home form since Newly introduced Year’s Day includes as many losses as wins in the league – six of each – and failures this season to beat Nottingham Forest (now 17th in the table), Fulham (15th) and Sunderland (19th).

Whatever that indicates about why Villa might be struggling at home, it’s clearly a problem and Emery, while positive about aspects of Villa’s play against the Black Cats, isn’t shying away from that.

One place where his team don’t come up against the exact challenges posed by some of their Premier League opponents is in the Champions League, where Villa have won two home games out of two in the league phase this season. Indeed, European competitions underpin the very notion of Villa Park as a fortress under Emery, who took Villa back into Europe ahead of the 2023/24 season.

Their last home loss in Europe was against Olympiacos in that year’s Conference League semi-finals. They won five out of six at home in the Champions League the next season, drawing the other, and won all seven of their home matches in their successful Europa League campaign in 2025/26.

While the idea of Villa being strong at home has endured, the evidence of it in the Premier League has not.

Industry observers note that villa’s home results in the league might have been short of their expected levels since before the summer, but there are differences between this season and last. Simply selling Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Emiliano Martinez, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Ollie Watkins fundamentally changed the picture at Villa Park.

It has been revealed that rogers and Tielemans were important players for breaking games open. Villa significantly outscored their expected goals value in periods of last season and goals from outside the penalty area were key.

They don’t have the same superpower this season; improving their chance creation is a must and that’s not quick or easy with any group of players, never mind a newly assembled and young team.

While the idea of Villa being strong at home has endured, the evidence of it in the Premier League has not.

Recent findings suggest that there’s also a looming, inconvenient possibility that’s beginning to sustain the weight of truth. Villa Park is a three-sided stadium this season because the North Stand – ordinarily full of home supporters – is being redeveloped behind one of the goals.

The difference is intangible, indefinable, but it’s there. Even the players can’t quantify it because half of them have never played at a four-sided Villa Park, but the vacant structure behind the goal makes for an unusual atmosphere.

Industry observers note that emery has no interest in excuses. The Villa manager is focused on process and progress, taking every challenge for what it is and finding the answers to the questions they pose.

Sources indicate that the North Stand redevelopment won’t be accepted as mitigation for poor home form in the dugout any more than it will in the other three stands, but Emery is no fool. He accepted after the Sunderland draw that Villa Park and the team who call it home are missing ‘something’ without the North Stand. It’s not an excuse, just another test.

Villa need to pass that test. Home results have been a hallmark of the Emery era. The manager himself has qualified for Europe every season since long before he succeeded Steven Gerrard.

Industry observers note that one win in six is a long way short of that standard. Emery’s meticulous and measured problem-solving has been called into action once more.

"Sacked in the morning, you're getting sacked in the morning...".

What on earth must Pochettino have been thinking as he stood at the edge of his technical area?

In distance terms, he was 3,800 miles from his last managerial assignment against Haiti in Cincinnati in the early hours of Wednesday morning UK time.

In difficulty levels, it must have felt significantly further than that.

By the final whistle, as Liverpool's gleeful supporters alternated between singing about the notion of Pochettino's immediate dismissal, United "going down" and celebrating "Poch is at the wheel", the Argentine head coach would have been starting to understand the scale of the task he has taken on by quitting his United States job.

He had just watched United be dismantled 4-0 by their oldest rivals, with Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card and two quickfire goals soon after representing just about the worst possible start imaginable to his reign as manager.

His team sit 19th in the 20-team Premier League after 11 games, already 20 points behind leaders Arsenal.

"Animals of the grass, we like to smell it and feel it," was the memorable phrase Pochettino came out with during Friday's pre-match media conference, explaining how he has missed the day-to-day nature of club football.

Listen to former United skipper Roy Keane's post-match summary of the loss on Sky Sports and a very different smell comes to mind.

For the record, it was the joint-worst result for any newly introduced United boss, matching the 4-0 loss Lal Hilditch suffered against Bolton in October 1926.

Hilditch lasted 30 games and never managed another team.

There were enough images of chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox broadcast during the game by Sky Sports to suggest there is a wider debate to be had about the quality of the players at Pochettino's disposal.

On Friday, Berrada said this season's squad was "fundamentally better" than the one which finished third last season. Few would agree with that, and presumably Keane is among the group who would challenge Berrada's assertion.

Pochettino, 54, shed tears of emotion when he explained his difficulty in deciding to quit the United States job and take up an opportunity at a club he has flirted with for the best part of a decade but, only now, has been given the chance to coach.

It was easy to imagine him being reduced to tears again as Sunday's debacle unfolded, a nightmare afternoon in Liverpool coming at the end of a chaotic week of travel.

He arrived to begin his newly introduced role as United head coach on Wednesday after agreeing a two-and-a-half-year contract.

The USA beat Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati in his final game in charge on Tuesday, with Pochettino flying directly to Manchester on a private jet after the game. He landed at about 11:30 GMT before heading to the club's Carrington training ground - and his feet have barely touched the floor since.

Mauricio Pochettino gives his post-match verdict on Liverpool v Man Utd.

Pochettino was bullish when speaking to the media after this 4-0 defeat.

Although he began his first answer by saying he went to referee Sam Barrott after the final whistle to "present his respect", he became increasingly more forceful in his view Leny Yoro should not have been sent off.

After dismissing the sorry statistic that United have conceded 19 goals in their latest six games, because he didn't want to talk about results and performances that occurred before he replaced Michael Carrick, he then used Yoro's red card as the prism through which his side's entire performance at Anfield should be judged.

It has been revealed that "What I learned from my players [today] is that they like to fight. They are committed with the team, with the club, and of course they want to win games," Pochettino said.

"Today we made an unbelievable effort. Today was a test. After eight minutes, 10 men, red card, concede the goal in this action. Do you think that is easy?

"Even the best team in the world playing like this in this situation, in our circumstance, maybe concede the four goals or maybe more.".

Recent findings suggest that it is a basic truth that Pochettino won six games this season as United States boss, twice as many as United have managed in 16 matches across all competitions. His new team have kept one clean sheet, against Azerbaijanis Sabah FK in the Champions League in September.

Pochettino's biggest selection call was to alter his defence by handing Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in almost 12 months.

It was a De Ligt misread of a bouncing ball that led to Yoro having to decide whether to foul Alexander Isak before he entered the penalty area.

Recent findings suggest that "It was clearly a foul and he was clearly the last man," said home boss Andoni Iraola, giving his reading from a Liverpool perspective. "Will he score? We will never know.".

Pochettino had a different opinion.

"If you go a minute and a half before, [Jeremy] Jacquet and [Bryan] Mbeumo and compare it..." he remarked, suggesting his team should have been awarded an earlier penalty.

"Yes, it's painful because it's 4-0. But for us to play 80 minutes with 10 men is unfair. We need to be critical but the action of Liverpool [player] was also a mistake, no? But we were punished and they were not. That is the truth.".

Pochettino takes his team, and his grievance, to Lisbon on Wednesday for a Champions League encounter with Sporting.

Sources indicate that after that, it is Brentford, Newcastle and Coventry in the Premier League. This, to an extent, was a game United and their fans, and even Keane probably, expected little from.

If they are still in the relegation zone after Coventry have left Old Trafford on 5 December, United really are in trouble.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

The home nations expect Fifa to be in a “different place” by the time they host the Women’s World Cup in 2035 after withdrawing their support for president Gianni Infantino earlier this year.

The joint bid from England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales was approved at the Fifa Congress on Monday, although it was the sole bidder to host the 48-team tournament and was voted through by acclamation.

The tournament will be the first World Cup to be held in the UK since England hosted the men’s World Cup in 1966, but it comes just months after the chair of the English FA, Debbie Hewitt, demanded an independent investigation into Infantino’s scrapped World Cup sell-off proposal and the Folarin Balogun affair, as well calls for further Fifa reform.

Infantino has retained the support required for re-election in March but cannot continue beyond 2031, and the FA’s director of women’s football Sue Day believes there will be significant change within Fifa as the home nations prepare to work alongside the governing body on staging the World Cup in 2035.

There have already been some challenges, with Fifa reportedly demanding tax-free status from ticket sales and broadcast and commercial partnerships, something that the UK government has not allowed when previously hosting major events such as the 2012 Olympics and will not offer to Uefa when they stage Euro 2028.

“There are two separate issues here, the concerns around the Fifa leadership and their proposals, and then this World Cup,” Day said on Monday.

“We very much want today to be about the excitement of this World Cup and we didn't want those concerns to get in the way of us trying to land the opportunity to put on this amazing tournament that we think can change the world of football.

Sources indicate that “By the time the tournament comes around, lots of things will have changed. We expect Fifa to be in a different place.

“We know that there is a brilliant team there right now, led by Jill Ellis [former USA manager, now Fifa’s Chief Football Officer], leading women’s football and we're really looking forward to working with them on developing the tournament.”.

Day also stated that the home nations hope to have a “strong influence” on the pricing of the tournament. Fifa were accused of “betrayal” and price gouging when the ticket prices were revealed for last summer’s men’s World Cup in North American last summer but tickets for the 2027 Women’s World Cup in Brazil will go on sale for as little as £4 next month.

But Fifa is targeting revenues of $4bn when it stages the first 48-team World Cup in 2031, in the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, and will be setting similar targets for the England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales bid.

Recent findings suggest that “At the moment, the model is absolutely that Fifa decides those things,” Day stated. “We will hope to be able to have a really strong influence on some of that because we know our audiences best.

“It’s going to be really notable to get the pricing right. We all know that we need to show the commercial viability of women’s football, and we want this to be an accessible tournament.”.

A 48-team Women’s World Cup would see the UK will host 104 matches across 39 days in 2035, in the largest single-sport event ever to be staged in the country, and Day said success for the tournament will be judged on its potential to transform society as well as what happens on the pitch.

“This is genuinely once in a lifetime, once in a generation,” Day mentioned. “There wouldn’t have been a World Cup on this soil since 1966, which would be nearly 70 years away.

“And so I think just collectively, I want us to grasp the opportunity of this moment and really build towards it and think of it as, it will be the most amazing tournament, but it's [also] a catalyst for growth and inspiration and something to springboard from.

Sources indicate that “I think we can change the world a little bit with the tournament and we should aim that high. Why wouldn't we aim that high?”.

David Moyes’ record-breaking night as Everton manager could not have been more miserable.

In his 593rd game as Toffees boss, Moyes broke Harry Catterick’s 75-year record for most games in the dugout.

But that was about the only positive he could take away from the Gtech Community Stadium, as high-flying Brentford battered ten-man Everton on an evening to forget for the 63-year-old Scotsman.

Daily Mail Sport's Bobby Manzi was at the Gtech Community Stadium on a torrid night for the Toffees...

The Bees can mix it with big boys.

Brentford, having missed out on European football on goal difference last season, are showing all the signs of being there or thereabouts again.

They climbed to sixth, leapfrogging Leeds — who have had far more praise lavished on them this season than Keith Andrews’ reliable side.

Brentford are disciplined with plenty of attacking flair, even with frontman and top goalscorer Igor Thiago suspended.

‘We've got a very competitive squad that strives to get better. If we continue with that mindset, we'll hopefully be in a good place.

‘I enjoyed us,’ he added about the performance. ‘I thought we were very good. We played with real bravery, courage and energy.’.

Brentford limited Everton to just three touches in the penalty area in the first half. They grabbed the game by the scruff of the neck and pinned their opponents back.

Recent findings suggest that jaidon Anthony was superb on the flank, providing two assists. Midfielder Vitaly Janelt capped off a brilliant display with a wonder strike from 25 yards, finding the top corner with his left foot.

It was a surprise to see Kevin Schade benched but this team is so cohesive, with more focus on the unit than any individual stars, that victory was light work for them.

Both of Keane Lewis-Potter’s goals had an element of fortune attached. But teams earn that luck when they manage ten shots in their opponents’ penalty area in just 45 minutes.

Lewis Potter starred at left-back, registering seven shots — the most of any player — and the joint-most touches in the opposition box. He was a menace and integral to every Brentford attack.

James Tarkowski endured a depressing return to his former club when he was shown the first Premier League red card of his career.

Sources indicate that it will split opinion, but in this day and age it is a clear red card. Although the Everton defender won the ball, his studs connected with Yehor Yarmolyuk’s shin on follow-through.

The speed and intensity of the tackle endangered his opponent. He had to go.

Recent findings suggest that referee Craig Pawson brandished a yellow, but a quick trip to the monitor saw it upgraded. Tarkowski ran down the tunnel before Pawson could even get the red card out of his pocket.

The home support enjoyed it, having taunted their former player throughout the first half.

To compound Everton’s misery, the first game of Tarkowski three-match ban is next weekend’s Merseyside derby.

Although Tarkowski won the ball, his studs connected with Yarmolyuk’s shin on follow-through.

A deflated Moyes had few complaints. ‘My feeling at the time was it wasn’t a red because James easily got to the ball before the Brentford player,’ the Everton boss remarked.

‘But after I saw it again, Tarky's boot is a bit higher than I'd like, so I can understand why the decision went against us.

‘We didn’t play well. Brentford did and credit to them. A bit unfortunate with the goals, it made it look even worse than it was.’.

Everton were unbeaten in four games at Brentford before this and their defeat came in the form of the sublime and the ridiculous.

Industry observers note that the first goal was all about Anthony undoing Everton on the left before Lewis-Potter was given far too much space to get his shot away. The deflection was unfortunate, but the defending was poor to begin with.

Sources indicate that tarkowski blocked an initial effort from Lewis-Potter for the second goal but the ball fell straight back to him, and Jake O’Brien helped his second attempt past Jordan Pickford. Once again, Everton should have done better and cleared the initial free-kick.

Portuguese forward Fabio Carvalho could not believe his luck when he added a late fourth, tapping in as Mathias Jensen’s corner flew straight past the congested pack at the near post.

Jack Grealish has returned to the Everton squad for the first time since being dropped for a breach of discipline.

Grealish last played in a 2-0 home defeat to Chelsea on 17 October, with the former England international punished for skipping training when he was not authorised to do so before the Carabao Cup tie with Newcastle.

He has not featured in four games - the first of which, against Arsenal, due to illness - with manager David Moyes not including him in previous matchday squads due to a lack of match fitness.

But after featuring in a behind-closed-doors friendly against Derby during the international break, Grealish has returned to the first-team fold and starts on the bench for Everton’s trip to Brentford on Monday night.

Moyes has preferred Merlin Rohl, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Tyrique George in the attacking midfield positions behind Thierno Barry, but Grealish could be in line for a substitute cameo.

Grealish apologised to fans after his friendly return to action, writing on his Instagram story: "Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training.

"I want to apologise to the fans and everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.

"I love playing for this club and can’t wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt. See you all soon.".

Grealish spent the 2025-26 season on loan at Everton before injury disrupted his spell, but he secured another temporary deal on transfer deadline day.

In his absence, Everton have won three of their last four matches to move up to sixth in the Premier League table, while also earning their spot in the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup.

HENRY WINTER: Bruno Fernandes has been a brilliant servant, but it's time to cut the cord at Manchester United

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United are under new management and need to be under new leadership on the field.
  • Bruno Fernandes has undeniably been a flickering beacon of brief hope for United in darkening times.
  • Even taking up the year’s option (unless to increase the player’s transfer fee) would be a retrograde step.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United are under new management and need to be under new leadership on the field.

Bruno Fernandes has undeniably been a flickering beacon of brief hope for United in darkening times. He’s been their Player of the Year in five of the last seven seasons, risen to 19th of their greatest scorers with 113 goals, has scored 75 times (24 pens, four free-kicks) and provided 74 assists in 240 Premier League games and is the reigning Footballer of the Year. But it’s undeniably time for the club to face reality, resist the urge to extend a contract which expires next summer and build for the future.

Even taking up the year’s option (unless to increase the player’s transfer fee) would be a retrograde step. Fernandes is 32, slowing up, and not now “best in class, 10 out of 10s” to borrow Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s catchphrase. He is not the most convincing of captains, moans too much and flaps his arms like a fledgling dove attempting to leave the nest.

Fernandes would never, ever be considered one of United’s elite captains in a strong, historic field that includes Sir Bobby Charlton, Roy Keane, Bryan Robson, Steve Bruce, Roger Byrne, Nemanja Vidic and Gary Neville, amongst others.

All are different; Neville was very vocal, Charlton led by example, but were united in their total commitment.

In a recent development, fernandes’ leadership qualities were brought into question when he openly criticised the tactics of Michael Carrick, effectively undermining him. That may not have been Fernandes’ intention when questioning the tactical approach against Como but it certainly didn’t help Carrick at a time when he needed players standing up to be counted, not standing up to his tactics in public. Such concerns – some of them legitimate – should have been aired in private.

Industry observers note that it demonstrated a lack of leadership from Fernandes, a lack of gratitude, too. Fernandes wouldn’t have been named the writers’ Footballer of the Year and the players’ Player of the Year without Carrick reviving United’s fortunes and their No. 8’s form last season.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

In receiving the writers’ award in May, Fernandes eulogised about the interim head coach, praising “the amazing job” he did in guiding United into the Champions League and saying Carrick possesses the “great character to become a top manager”.

Such an endorsement from such an influential figure at the club, effectively the voice of the dressing-room, undoubtedly contributed to Ineos and the Glazers appointing Carrick to the permanent role.

Industry observers note that bruno’s voice is powerful. That is why it was damaging when he spoke out against Carrick’s tactics. “Lies,” was Bruno’s reaction to some of the interpretation of his words but mud stuck.

Industry observers note that carrick questioned individuals’ running stats – without naming Fernandes – and then dropped him for the game against Bournemouth. United need real leaders. In fairness to Fernandes, there are plenty of stories of the good work he does behind the scenes.

Recent findings suggest that who would inherit the armband in the unlikely event that Carrick’s successor, Mauricio Pochettino, was brave and looked to the future? Matthijs de Ligt, an Ajax captain at 18, would be a strong contender were it not for his back problems. Senne Lammens represents United admirably on and off the field, and was one of only two who emerged with reputation intact from Anfield.

The other was Kobbie Mainoo. It might seem a leap of faith in one so young, still only 21, but Mainoo could perform the duties until a more experienced leader was recruited by the club that once bought Keane, Bruce, Vidic etc. (All of this is a reminder of United’s need to buy leaders, powerful characters as well as good players).

Industry observers note that mainoo’s one of the few deserving of his place currently. He’s also an academy graduate, a local lad, and a link to great home-grown generations. Fans would love that re-affirmation of United’s identity. It would be quite a statement by Pochettino.

Mainoo has only minimal captaincy experience against Bayern Munich in 2017 (as a kid) and successfully with England Under-19s in 2023. More recently, more pertinently, Mainoo acted like a leader against Roma on November 3 when others were losing their discipline.

It has been revealed that it’s still too early, of course, and Mainoo is still developing but he could do the honours on a temporary basis in the unlikely event that United cut the cord with Fernandes. But a recruitment department incapable of making strong decisions and buying “best in class” – they were not in the running when Elliot Anderson and Morgan Rogers were available in the summer - may be tempted to go for the easy option of keeping Fernandes, rather than step into a upcoming era.

Sources indicate that henry Winter is one of football's most popular and respected writers. Previously the Chief Football Writer for The Times and a Football Correspondent for The Daily Telegraph, his work now primarily features on his Substack. He has also lauched his own podcast 'The Winter View'.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, there are two non-negotiables for Chelsea managers.
  • Just as Spurs broke their Stamford Bridge hoodoo a few weeks ago, Leeds secured their first win at Chelsea since 1999 by humiliating the hosts after falling a goal behind.
  • It was 67 long years since Chelsea had last lost at home to Tottenham and Leeds in the same season, and Alonso was left in no doubt about how seriously supporters take that as his team were loudly booed and he was heckled.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, there are two non-negotiables for Chelsea managers. Do not lose at home to Tottenham Hotspur and do not lose at home to Leeds United. But Xabi Alonso has now completed the nightmare double.

Just as Spurs broke their Stamford Bridge hoodoo a few weeks ago, Leeds secured their first win at Chelsea since 1999 by humiliating the hosts after falling a goal behind.

It was 67 long years since Chelsea had last lost at home to Tottenham and Leeds in the same season, and Alonso was left in no doubt about how seriously supporters take that as his team were loudly booed and he was heckled.

Cole Palmer stormed down the tunnel at full time, ignoring the advice of Chelsea’s so-called “cultural architect” Willie Isa to applaud the remaining home fans, and shrugging off the attention of injured striker João Pedro.

Having been left out of the last England squad, Palmer was largely anonymous for Chelsea but he was not alone and Alonso is already facing similar questions to his predecessors about the team’s mentality.

Sources indicate that “I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment, mentally,” Alonso mentioned. “When we receive a punch, we didn’t recover that strong, that tough enough and today that was my feeling.

“The fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high and we feel sorry for them. For sure, it’s not the easiest moment. It’s a fragile moment, but we need to work together and stick together because there is still a long way to go.”.

Alonso is yet to name the same starting XI for successive league games and there appears to be no discernible initiative or style of play.

Injuries have contributed to Chelsea’s unremarkable start to the season under Alonso – and Moisés Caicedo was forced off early in the first half – but the problems run deeper than the treatment table.

Alonso’s defence has now conceded 20 goals, which has contributed to Chelsea losing five league games already – more than Manchester United. In between three defeats in their last four league games, Chelsea were also knocked out of the Carabao Cup.

Recent findings suggest that the Spaniard had answered questions about Chelsea’s identity, or lack of it, by saying he wanted his team to be competitive. But they were anything but against a Leeds side who had seven more shots than their hosts and five more on target.

It is hard to fathom how, through all the chopping and changing, Wesley Fofana still starts games for Chelsea in defence. It was his pathetic attempted header, which bounced backwards towards his own goal, that contributed to Noah Okafor’s first goal.

Josh Acheampong also got himself into a mess and Okafor was somehow able to squeeze a shot past goalkeeper Emi Martínez despite having three Chelsea players around him.

Chelsea had taken the lead through striker Emmanuel Emegha, on his first start for the club, but from that moment on they were second best with Leeds pair Ethan Ampadu and Ao Tanaka running the middle of the park.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin had hit the crossbar and failed to find the net with three more presentable opportunities in the first half, but he took his chance from the penalty spot eight minutes after the break.

Morgan Rogers had argued that James Justin’s shot hit him too far up his arm for it to be a penalty, but a VAR check upheld referee Michael Oliver’s decision and Calvert-Lewin kept his cool.

That should have been the moment that shook Chelsea into action and prompted a response but, instead, Alonso’s team fell apart and he was unable to provoke a shift in momentum from the touchline.

Just five minutes after Calvert-Lewin had put Leeds ahead, Okafor effectively sealed the victory by firing the ball into the net after Chelsea had failed to deal with a long throw into their penalty area.

According to recent reports, noah Okafor's brace helps seal Leeds' first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge since 1999! 💥 https://t.co/UAmsJziJmZ.

According to recent reports, “I can’t wait to be on the sofa with coffee and cake and also watch this game back because it was a really good game,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds head coach, mentioned. “I was a bit disappointed even at half-time when it was just a draw, because I think we were the better side from the first to the last.”.

John Terry still works with Chelsea’s academy and it might be worth Alonso getting the former captain to speak to the club’s senior players about how to defend and compete. Whatever has been done on the training pitch so far has not worked.

It has been revealed that alonso’s substitutes are yet to register a single goal or assist in the league this season and his changes failed to make any sort of impact here. For the visitors, however, two substitutes combined to score their fourth goal in time added on for stoppages.

Harry Wilson played in Brenden Aaronson and, from a tight angle, he managed to find the back of the net by sending the ball through the legs of Martínez.

The home stands were already half-empty by that point, but some supporters hung around to show their displeasure and Palmer could not contain his anger.

It has been revealed that we know what the history of this game is like and what the fans expect - we know they have wanted a win here for a long time. It’s right we can enjoy this performance.

It has been revealed that frank’s start to life at Palace begins with defeat but an improved display. Coventry are up to 13th with their fourth win of the season.

Another home win for Tottenham, who managed the game well and introduced a new star to the Premier League in Williams-Barnett.

Industry observers note that what a day for Leeds. They scored four and it could have been more. For Chelsea, they lost their way when Caicedo went off and without Joao Pedro, they have lost their spark in attack.

Bournemouth make it nine wins in a row in all competitions after doing enough in the first half to get the job done.

Leeds finish the match in style as Aaronson puts the seal on an impressive away day.

Recent findings suggest that it’s all over and Sunderland deservedly leave with a point. Villa will be very disappointed by their display.

What was I saying in the last post?! The home side are on the attack Thomas-Asante pokes a shot at goal and forces Henderson into a save but hits his own player McNeil, who bundles the ball in the net.

Can Chelsea stage a late fightback? Will we get a winner between Coventry and Palace?

Needing a goal, Emery makes a bold decision to take off Villa’s top scorer and bring on Madjo.

Despite the two-goal lead and the magnificent debut performance of Luca Williams-Barnett, the home support has remained subdued throughout the afternoon.

At times, the shouts of two children sat just behind the press box feel like by far the loudest noise in the stadium - although that might just be proximity.

Much quieter half at the CBS Arena but Palace are more likely to get a third goal.

According to recent reports, this has gone from bad to worse for Chelsea. One supporter near the dug-outs was so angry at Leeds scoring a third goal that he got up and screamed his displeasure at manager Xabi Alonso.

Villa’s fans are now chanting loudly for substitute John McGinn to be introduced.

Villa need an injection of energy.

Recent findings suggest that everything Luca Williams-Barnett touches is turning to gold today. He has a goal to his name already, and adds an assist just six minutes into the second half.

Williams-Barnet gets one-on-one with Furlong and gets past him with ease before firing a cross for Solanke to finish.

The whistle blows for the second half around the grounds. What will the second 45 minutes have for us?

Sunderland have defended resolutely and caused Villa’s back-four some problems in the rare moments they have attacked.

Unai Emery marched into the dressing room after the half-time whistle and has much to ponder.

Chelsea just stopped playing after taking the lead.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card was a pivotal moment early in Mauricio Pochettino's first game as Manchester United boss.
  • It handed Liverpool the initiative at Anfield, and Andoni Iraola's players took advantage by scoring two goals in quick succession.
  • Was there a case for the video assistant referee (VAR) to suggest it should be downgraded to a yellow?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ngumoha stars as Liverpool thrash 10-man Man Utd.

Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card was a pivotal moment early in Mauricio Pochettino's first game as Manchester United boss.

It handed Liverpool the initiative at Anfield, and Andoni Iraola's players took advantage by scoring two goals in quick succession.

Should it have been a red card though?

Was there a case for the video assistant referee (VAR) to suggest it should be downgraded to a yellow?

Let's take a look at the incident, and what a referee takes into account before showing a red for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

Photographers at Anfield captured the sequence of events - from challenge to red card.

Photographers at Anfield captured the sequence of events - from challenge to red card.

Photographers at Anfield captured the sequence of events - from challenge to red card.

Photographers at Anfield captured the sequence of events - from challenge to red card.

Photographers at Anfield captured the sequence of events - from challenge to red card.

Ronald Araujo played a long ball upfield for Alexander Isak to run on to.

Isak took a touch, before Yoro bundled into the back of the Sweden international and brought him down.

Referee Sam Barrott did not hesitate, giving the foul and sending off Yoro.

Was there doubt that Isak would have taken control of the ball? If so, it should only be a caution.

There are four key considerations for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity:.

distance between the offence and the goal.

likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball.

location and number of defenders and attackers.

As Isak was running directly towards goal in a central position, and there was no covering defender, three of the factors were satisfied.

The question is about the "likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball".

The Liverpool striker took a heavy touch, which moved the ball a few yards ahead of him.

The touch came before contact from Yoro, so there is no case that the challenge caused Isak to over-run the ball.

Recent findings suggest that the referee and the VAR, John Brooks, must therefore assess whether Isak would definitely have got to the ball ahead of Senne Lammens. And that if he had, it would have been a good scoring chance.

If there is any doubt, then it should not be a red card.

It is a borderline case, and as such the VAR would not be expected to intervene for a clear and obvious error.

Likewise, if the referee had shown a yellow the VAR would not get involved.

Former Liverpool and England midfielder Danny Murphy, who is a pundit on Sunday's Match of the Day, said there was "no doubt" about the red card.

Former Manchester United defender Gary Neville also agreed with the decision.

According to recent reports, "Leny Yoro has to cover and he doesn't," Neville stated on Sky Sports. "He reacts late and his anticipation is poor.

It has been revealed that "It's so clumsy from Yoro. It's naivety, he just needs to get off the pitch. You're not going to get that turned around, no chance.".

But for Liverpool boss Iraola the decision is not up for debate.

According to recent reports, "I think he's the last man, no?" he said. "It's a clear foul and a red card, yes?

Did Liverpool 'get lucky' with red card decision?

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes felt it should not have been a red card and said the decision had a detrimental impact on the game.

"It's one that needs to be looked at," Fernandes told Sky Sports.

Recent findings suggest that "We have far too many meetings with the referees for this to happen to us again. The last one against Chelsea [when Lisandro Martinez was sent off], you can give it as a red card and it was probably a second yellow also. Today, you can't give a red card.

"It's very clear they show us if the player is not in control of the ball, it's never a red card.

Industry observers note that "Isak kicks the ball forward, the ball goes into the hands of Senne. Isak has got no control of the ball, he has no chance to get on the ball. He puts his leg across to try to get some advantage from Leny. I can understand the fall, but it's never a red card.

"There are too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR taking so long to see to make a mistake like this that can change the game.

"It's not because of them we conceded the goal from the free-kick, but it changes the game completely.".

Pochettino, meanwhile, was frustrated by what he perceived as inconsistency in the decision-making of the officials.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss felt his new team should have been awarded a penalty moments before Yoro was sent off, after Jeremy Jacquet went shoulder to shoulder with Bryan Mbeumo.

"It's difficult to accept that because it was a foul under my view and for me was a penalty," Pochettino told Match of the Day.

"Look how everything changes if that action was a red card and a foul, I think we need to review. When I played football that situation is normal. The action against Mbeumo, if that [Yoro foul on Isak] was a red card then that was a penalty.".

'We have too many referees' - Fernandes disagrees with Yoro red.

There have been a couple of very similar cases this season.

Brighton's Pascal Struijk was sent off at Sunderland through a VAR review after he brought down Wilson Isidor.

The Seagulls successfully appealed against that red card on the grounds that there was clear doubt that Isidor would have taken control of the ball before it ran through to goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

Could Manchester United appeal against Yoro's red card? There's nothing to lose by doing so.

Despite the Football Association regulatory commission unanimously ruling the Struijk red card was wrong, the Premier League's key match incidents panel voted the VAR intervention was a correct call on a split 3-2 vote.

Ipswich's Issa Diop avoided a VAR red card for a foul on James McAtee against Nottingham Forest, when the referee disagreed with the video official, and believed there was a covering defender. Forest boss Oliver Glasner was adamant it had been a clear goalscoring opportunity.

It was the same referee, Thomas Bramall, for both of those incidents.

Sources indicate that that shows just how subjective such decisions can be. It is often rare to get a real consensus.

Yoro can count himself a little unfortunate to get the red card.

Industry News: FIFA presidential election 2027: Infantino facing Diallo and Tashima — could an alliance change everything?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Three men are vying for one of the most powerful positions in sports when delegates from more than 200 member nations of FIFA, soccer's global governing body, cast their ballots at the FIFA presidential election, to be held in Rabat on March 18, 2027.
  • It has been revealed that gianni Infantino was first elected FIFA president in February 2016, promising greater transparency and a fresh start in the wake of the corruption scandals that marked the Sepp Blatter era.
  • It has been revealed that during his decade in office, the 56-year-old Swiss has built a global network of support.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three men are vying for one of the most powerful positions in sports when delegates from more than 200 member nations of FIFA, soccer's global governing body, cast their ballots at the FIFA presidential election, to be held in Rabat on March 18, 2027. DW looks at the field of candidates.

It has been revealed that gianni Infantino was first elected FIFA president in February 2016, promising greater transparency and a fresh start in the wake of the corruption scandals that marked the Sepp Blatter era. Under Infantino's leadership, FIFA's revenues have continued to grow, the Club World Cup has been revamped, and the men's World Cup has been expanded to include 48 teams.

It has been revealed that during his decade in office, the 56-year-old Swiss has built a global network of support. Infantino enjoys significant backing in Africa, South America, and large parts of Asia — a result of multi-billion-dollar development programs and financial grants provided to national associations. Many smaller member associations view him as a president who takes their interests more seriously than his predecessors did.

Sources indicate that at the same time, critics accuse Infantino of consolidating power within the organization around himself. During his tenure, oversight and control bodies have been restructured multiple times, and key positions have been filled with his own loyalists.

Sources indicate that infantino's ostentatious closeness to political leaders has also sparked debate — whether exemplified by his conduct during the World Cup in Qatar, his tight ties to Saudi Arabia or his public appearances alongside US President Donald Trump (though that relationship is noted to have cooled significantly after the 2026 World Cup). Detractors accuse him of seeking proximity to authoritarian rulers and intermingling political interests too closely with football.

According to recent reports, A failed initiative to grant private investors a larger stake in lucrative FIFA competitions (FIFA Forward Enterprise) has also placed Infantino under considerable pressure. As the FIFA election approaches, he faces the prospect of legal challenges; European football's governing body UEFA is aiming to take action over the investment proposal, while other critics are calling for an investigation by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

It has been revealed that however, his time in office has brought many of FIFA's 211 member associations additional development funding and other revenue. This makes him the man to beat in the March vote.

Philippe Diallo is Europe's candidate. The 63-year-old, who was elected president of the French Football Federation in 2023, is seen as an experienced sports administrator with a pragmatic and measured leadership style.

He has the backing of UEFA, as well as many of its 55 member associations, including the German Football Association (DEB).

"Philippe Diallo stands for a version of football that embraces responsibility and tackles future challenges with determination," DFB President Bernd Neuendorf said in a statement announcing the German FA's position.

"We want a FIFA that serves the sport in the interest of all its member associations. That is why we support Philippe Diallo with great conviction.".

Diallo is positioning himself as a clear alternative to Infantino. His supporters see him as a candidate who stands for sound leadership, transparency, and a stronger dialogue with member associations. Unlike the incumbent, however, he lacks a global network of allies.

According to recent reports, the third man in the race is Kozo Tashima. The 68-year-old was president of the Japan Football Association (JFA) from 2016 to 2024 and has been one of the most influential officials in Asia for decades.

During a press conference in the Japanese capital Tokyo on Friday, Tashima mentioned the words "integrity, fairness, trust and transparency" several times in explaining his decision to run.

"I just don't only want to be the FIFA president, my intention is to make FIFA better," he said.

In a recent development, "Being the president is the shortcut to making that happen. I just want to clean up the federation and make it a fair organization. I want to help rebuild the whole organization.".

Tashima also acknowledged that failing to have won the endorsement of any of the regional confederations — the Asian Football Confederation is supporting Infantino — makes him a longshot to win the election.

In a recent development, but he could still play a key role in the outcome. At a press conference on Tuesday, Diallo said he intended to reach out to Tashima to "unite forces" to defeat Infantino. Tashima hasn't ruled out the notion.

"We do share some moral or ethical positions, so he's a great person to team up with," he said.

"Diallo is also very strict in governance and he does have a lot of experience in management," he added.

However, Tashima also noted that he hadn't had any thoughts of withdrawing from the race.

If Infantino's challengers do manage to join forces in some way, they might just stand a chance of upsetting the highly favored incumbent.

Breaking: Pioneer or coach-eater? The complex world of Pozzo's Watford

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1678 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gino Pozzo (left) has presided over 25 permanent Watford bosses in 14 years, with Alessio Dionisi the latest to take charge of the Hornets.
  • A week is noted to be a long time in football, and few clubs offer a more compelling test of that theory than Watford.
  • It has been 14 years since the Pozzo family completed their takeover of the Hornets and Alessio Dionisi's dismissal leaves them searching for the 25th permanent boss of their tenure.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gino Pozzo (left) has presided over 25 permanent Watford bosses in 14 years, with Alessio Dionisi the latest to take charge of the Hornets.

A week is noted to be a long time in football, and few clubs offer a more compelling test of that theory than Watford.

It has been 14 years since the Pozzo family completed their takeover of the Hornets and Alessio Dionisi's dismissal leaves them searching for the 25th permanent boss of their tenure.

The Italian's dismissal was announced on Sunday lunchtime with his 18th and final game in charge proving to be the 4-0 defeat by Sheffield United less than 24 hours earlier.

An average incumbency of about 210 days per manager has generated all too familiar headlines of the Hornets seeking a new face in the dugout, but is there method in the madness?

Pozzo court case in Spain adds to unrest at Watford.

Watford sack boss Dionisi after 18 games.

Brereton Diaz double leads Blades to win over Watford.

The Hornets were taken over by the Pozzos on 29 June 2012, with the family having also owned Serie A side Udinese since 1986.

Gino Pozzo has been in charge ever since, overseeing an ownership model rooted in a vast global scouting network famed for buying low and selling high, with Brazil internationals Richarlison and Joao Pedro among those flipped for major fees.

In the 61-year-old's first seven years, the club shifted from existential crisis to FA Cup finalists.

Under Javi Gracia, they came close to qualifying for Europe through the Premier League in 2019 before arriving at a Wembley showpiece where they came up second best to Manchester City.

But it proved to be a peak from which they have steadily spiralled.

Relegation from the Premier League a year later was followed by an immediate return - but a further relegation from which they have not recovered.

Last season's 16th-place finish was their lowest in the second tier under Pozzo - with a frequent turnover of manager seemingly utilised as a failed antidote to their stagnation.

That sense of inertia - and a poor start to 2026-27 which has left them 21st in the Championship, has brightened the spotlight on the owner and his methods.

With more than a third of the league season complete, Watford are one place outside of the Championship relegation zone.

After back-to-back hammerings by Burnley and Cardiff City in October, former Hornets midfielder Tom Ince remarked he feared for the club he left at the end of last season.

"There are a lot of different beliefs on how the football club should move forward." Ince told the 72+ podcast.

He pointed to Gracia ending his second spell in charge last season after only three months - and with the club four points off the Championship play-offs - as a "big, big problem" that summed up their instability.

"There is so much control away from the manager at that club that it will always be an glitch," noted Ince. "The players don't see the manager as the focal point. He [Pozzo] is the one in control.

"That is always going to be a problem because you can't look at a manager and not have any fear [in them].

"I look at Watford, the players in the dressing room. You have a lot of young players, who have not played in England before. When this hiring and firing of managers is going on, they're just like 'OK, onto the next one [manager]'.".

Too many cooks at Watford - Ince.

While Ince, now at League Two side Tranmere Rovers, added his respect for positives to Pozzo's practise, he is not alone in speaking out about the board's influence.

Speaking on No Tippy Tappy Football,, external former England boss Sam Allardyce said he had turned down the chance to manage the club prior to the appointment of Nigel Pearson in 2019.

"I got interviewed at Watford before Nigel [Pearson]," Allardyce revealed.

"[Sir] Elton [John] rang me up and said, 'Come on, Sam, take the job'.

"It was very nice having a phone call from Elton John, I must admit. But I met with the board, sat in the boardroom, and went, 'I can't take this job'.

"They were telling me what to do, saying, 'Play this way, play that player, this manager's not been playing that player' and so on.".

Gino Pozzo has been Watford's owner since 2012.

Ince and Allardyce's remarks came after former Watford owner John noted he was "upset and disappointed" by the club's form after their 4-0 defeat by Burnley.

"I really feel for the supporters who have to watch this," he wrote in response to a club post on Instagram.

When supporter group The 1881 Movement published an open letter declaring a "complete loss of confidence" in Pozzo, the Italian, who has rarely spoken publically had no choice but to.

His meeting with prominent supporter Roy Moore was recorded and released as an extraordinary 114-minute podcast episode by the club's official channels.

Watford fans state 'loss of confidence' in ownership.

Elton John 'upset and disappointed' with Watford form.

"I don't have a social presence, I don't like to speak publicly, I don't enjoy that, I don't think it's productive for the work we do," Pozzo explained.

Industry observers note that "I don't like to answer to speculation, because a lot of the people that are out there want a bit of visibility for themselves. Unfortunately social media creates this sort of character.

Sources indicate that "I'm not expecting everybody to understand our model. In order to compete with the other clubs, we need to be something different. Otherwise we would not even be in the Championship right now.".

Though Udinese is formally owned by his father, Giampaolo, Pozzo is still heavily involved in the management of the Italian club.

It is for this reason that he dismisses a reputation for devouring head coaches - Udinese boss Kosta Runjaic was, until his sacking earlier this month,, external Serie A's longest-serving manager having been appointed before the 2024-25 season.

According to recent reports, "I tend to have a very good relationship with the coach, because the coach is a fundamental part," said Pozzo. "Whenever we sign a coach there is normally strong bond and good idea and we share that.

In a recent development, "It [sacking managers] has cost me a lot, I know I'm not looking good. Every time I change a coach, it's not a good image. But I cannot stand the fact that my image is worth more than the club's results. I put the club in front.".

Watford have finished outside the top 10 in each of their past four Championship seasons.

Before the win over Charlton Athletic on 17 October, some supporters tried to orchestrate a protest against Pozzo's ownership.

It is a far cry from the high point of his reign, when a tifo bearing his name was unfurled at Vicarage Road.

Tom Bodell, a Hornets supporter who contributes to the Watford Buzz podcast, mentioned outside views of the club being a "basket case" who change manager two or three times a season was "the tip of the iceberg".

"We've seen over certainly three years, possibly five years now, a real reduction in overheads and outlay on the football side," he stated.

In a recent development, "This summer we saw quite a bit of talent leave for reasonable money and next to nothing spent. We paid a fee for the goalkeeper Federico Ravaglia, but I believe that was it.

"Everybody else was either a loan, a free transfer or came from Udinese. So, you know, passing money from one pocket to the other on the same pair of jeans.".

Bodell said chief executive and chairman Scott Duxbury had failed to deliver on promises of signing players with proven EFL experience, with concerns also mounting over the downgrading of the club's academy.

"There have been enough instances now of supporters feeling that they've been at best let down, at worst kind of misled or lied to that it is very hard to rebuild that trust," stated Bodell.

"They [the owners] are at very real risk of leaving us in a worse position than when they arrived and I think that is probably the thing that has tipped people into action.".

Alessio Dionisi lost more than half of his games in charge of Watford.

But while the optics of Pozzo's model and methods have hit an all-time low for English observers, his image in his homeland is assured, according to Vincenzo Credendino, a journalist with Sport Italia.

"The [Pozzo] business model is a winning model because he is not an American billionaire or an Arab Sultan, he has to apply the model he worked on to buy young players and sell them," remarked Credendino.

"This is a model that allows Gino Pozzo with Udinese to compete in the Champions League, and reaching high levels at least in Italian football.

Sources indicate that "If you look at many teams in Serie A, you can find many players who came out from Udinese. Piotr Zielinski, at Inter Milan is just one example.".

For the frustration of Hornets' fans, it is a point that is difficult to deny.

Rodrigo de Paul, Alexis Sanchez, Alex Meret and Juan Cuadrado are all examples of players bought low and sold high at Udinese.

While at Watford, Abdoulaye Doucoure and Odion Ighalo are further examples of players to bring money into the Hertfordshire club.

"When you speak about Gino Pozzo, you are speaking about a piece of history." added Credendino.

Sources indicate that "He's really pioneering. He has visions of the future. He has agreed a new perspective about many things, and many clubs look at his model and decided to make something similar.".

It has been revealed that so, is there method in the madness? Undoubtedly. But for those associated with Watford, the madness alone might prove to be Pozzo's lasting legacy.
