Bruno Fernandes says he has shelved talks over a new contract because it is not the “right moment” for discussions over his future as Manchester United captain.

Fernandes, 32, is out of contract next summer although United have a 12-month option to extend his deal to 2028.

The Portugal midfielder is understood to have rejected two contract offers from United since the summer but said all his focus needs to be on trying to help the team out of their current plight.

United head into Sunday’s game against Liverpool at Anfield second from bottom in the Premier League.

“We spoke about the contract at the end of last season,” Fernandes told Sky Sports.

“We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.

“The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.”.

Fernandes said claims he wants more money or a longer-term deal on offer are incorrect and that if finances were the issue he would have left Old Trafford before now. The captain has previously rejected lucrative offers from Saudi Arabia.

“The club offered me a latest contract, so I think that, from their side, reveals that they want me to stay,” he mentioned.

Sources indicate that “There’s no negotiations ongoing, but I’ve seen people saying that ‘He’s asked for more money, he’s asked for more years’. If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here.

It has been revealed that “I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

“Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

It has been revealed that “The thing is, I’ve always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it’s time for me to move on, I will move on.

“I’m not going to be the player that I’ve seen many in this time at Manchester United. They’re going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club states, ‘Bruno, it’s time to part ways’, I’m going to be the first one walking out the door.”.

United chief executive Omar Berrada noted of Fernandes on Friday that it was “true that we’re having conversations about his upcoming contract” but that the club preferred “to keep that private”.

Having been voted PFA Player of the Year last season, Fernandes’ form has dropped off this term like that of the team.

He was dropped for the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth in the wake of a 4-1 drubbing by Como when he criticised the tactics and approach of then head coach Michael Carrick.

Mauricio Pochettino, Carrick’s successor, confirmed on Friday that Fernandes would remain as captain.

Fernandes said the United fans had been “far too patient with us” and hopes Pochettino - who wanted to bring the Portuguese to Spurs in 2019 - will bring a fresh energy.

“He’s someone that likes to bring a very good energy to the team, someone very positive, very strong, strict, said it straight away that he won’t allow us to not give him what he demands from the team, from each player,” Fernandes said.

“He wants the club to succeed so much, he wants to win games, and that’s pretty clear and obvious by the way he and his staff speak and want us to improve.

Sources indicate that “Obviously [in 2019] I was a very young player that was eager to come to the Premier League. They had [Harry] Kane there, they had Dele Alli, Son, the chance of playing with those players in front was very attractive.”.

Recent findings suggest that watch Newcastle in their current, post-Bruno Guimaraes iteration and the same problem jumps off the screen. The energy is still there, and St James’ Park can still generate an intimidating atmosphere, but unless the team go direct, things slow to a crawl when the ball reaches midfield.

Losing Guimaraes was always going to leave a dent in the armoury, but the extent to which Newcastle have lost their forward punch is worrying from a black-and-white perspective. And the underlying numbers confirm what supporters were worried about.

According to Gradient Sports data, Newcastle have completed the fifth-lowest number of line-breaking passes in the Premier League this season.

Guimaraes lived for disguising passes through narrow gaps, taking two or three opponents out of the game with a single touch.

Without him, Newcastle’s midfield is a creativity bottleneck. They at the moment post the lowest completion rate for 'midfield line-breaking passes' across the entire division. Instead of playing forward, the ball gets stuck under players' feet, the tempo dies, and opposition defences are given plenty of time to shuffle across and set their shape.

Not a single Newcastle player sits inside the top 38 line-breaking passers in the Premier League this campaign, as per Gradient data.

Nico Gonzalez is the closest they have, coming in at 39th. He's tidy enough on the ball and offers some progression, but the data indicates he is only a partial answer.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Gonzalez has attempted just four passes designed to break multiple lines all season, finding his man with only one of them. His numbers against the opposition's back four are similarly modest, having completed just one defensive line-breaking pass from three attempts. He keeps things ticking, but he isn't slicing teams open.

It has been revealed that that hesitation in the middle is costing Newcastle badly further up the pitch. In Will Osula and Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Matthias Jaissle has two forwards who are quick off the mark and desperate to stretch games by spinning in behind.

Both players thrive on early, vertical service into space but at the moment, they are making the runs only to watch the ball get recycled sideways back towards the centre-halves. Until someone behind them starts making those aggressive passes, Newcastle are leaving weapons unused.

Nico Gonzalez - Newcastle - 2026/27 Premier League.

Arthur Avom - Lorient - 2026/27 Ligue 1.

In a recent development, sporting director Ross Wilson doesn't need to break the bank to sort it out this winter, either. In France, Lorient’s Arthur Avom has quietly been putting up the exact numbers Newcastle are crying out for.

In a recent development, the 21-year-old Cameroon international is decisive and remarkably accurate. Compare his output directly with Newcastle's current midfielders and the difference is night and day.

It has been revealed that avom has completed three out of three multiple line-breaking passes this season, alongside seven from 10 when attempting to thread balls through the opposition’s defensive line. Just as eye-catching is his overall efficiency because Avom has completed 90 per cent of his line-breaking passes so far this campaign - the same ratio managed by Barcelona's former Ballon d'Or winner, Rodri.

Granted, Avom is playing in Ligue 1, not the Premier League or LaLiga, but matching the gold standard of European holding midfielders for progression in any division is no small feat.

Avom won't cost a fortune as his contract at Lorient expires at the end of the season, putting the French club in a weak negotiating position ahead of the January window.

Recent findings suggest that even if Lorient hold an undisclosed option to extend his deal by a further year, a winter fee would be comfortably within reach. Guimaraes can never be replaced like-for-like, of course, but if Newcastle want their attack firing again, bringing in Avom - or a player of his ilk - is a no-brainer.

In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers.

It has been revealed that who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S.

Industry observers note that although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling.

Leonid meteor shower thrills stargazers worldwide with colorful sky show (photos/video)

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1212 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Leonid meteor shower put on quite the show this week, with bright, colorful meteors thrilling stargazers worldwide and we've got the photos to prove it.
  • The annual meteor shower peaked overnight on Nov.
  • Leonids occur when Earth passes through debris left behind by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Leonid meteor shower put on quite the show this week, with bright, colorful meteors thrilling stargazers worldwide and we've got the photos to prove it.

The annual meteor shower peaked overnight on Nov. 17-18, with photographers braving chilly temperatures, clouds and even fog in hopes of catching the perfect shot. And for some, their patience certainly paid off.

Leonids occur when Earth passes through debris left behind by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years. As tiny pieces of comet debris enter Earth's atmosphere at speeds of up to 44 miles (71 kilometers) per second, they burn up, producing bright streaks of light.

The meteor shower is also famous for producing some of the most spectacular meteor storms in history. In fact, this year marks the 60th anniversary of the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966, when observers reported an astonishing 40 meteors per second at the peak. To mark the occasion, we spoke to people who witnessed the extraordinary event first-hand and you can read their remarkable accounts in our special feature.

According to recent reports, but back to the present! Let's take a look at some of the best photographs and videos captured during this year's impressive display.

Photographer Austin Rebello drove several hours to Nubble Lighthouse in York, Maine, to meet up with fellow astrophotographer Rob Wright and hopefully capture a Leonid or two.

"I specifically drove a few hours up there for hopes of capturing exactly this, as the radiant of the Leonids rose behind the lighthouse," Rebello told Space.com in an email.

"My friend and I were lucky enough to also see it with our eyes, and it was definitely a top 3 meteor for me, as it was even bright enough to briefly cast shadows.".

Rebello also revealed on X that the meteor left behind a vibrant blue trail that remained visible to the naked eye for more than 30 seconds.

Fellow astrophotographer Rob Wright was also at Nubble Lighthouse that night, where he captured the lingering trail of a particularly bright meteor on camera for an incredible 12 minutes, according to a post on X.

"Turns out the smoke from the bright meteor early this morning was visible on camera for TWELVE (12) MINUTES just lingering there," Wright wrote on X.

Turns out the smoke from the bright meteor early this morning was visible on camera for TWELVE (12) MINUTES just lingering there. I was able to make a rough timelapse video to show this. -- November 18, 2026 York, Maine https://t.co/pm9htHcMm3November 18, 2026.

This phenomenon is known as a persistent meteor train and is created when a bright meteor leaves behind a trail of ionized gas that continues to glow long after the meteor itself has disappeared. These ghostly trails usually fade relatively swiftly, but some, like this one, can persist for several minutes. They can twist and change shape as they're carried along by winds high in Earth's atmosphere, according to the BBC Sky at Night Magazine.

Meanwhile, over Deming, Newly introduced Mexico, photographer Greg Gage had to contend with rather less favorable conditions as clouds and unexpected fog rolled in during the meteor shower's peak.

"While it was perfectly clear when I set up the camera, the night turned out to be mostly cloudy with some light fog," Gage told Space.com in an email.

In a recent development, "But it was just a thin veil and made for some interesting effects. I did catch one meteor through the fog.".

But the fog wasn't the only surprise Gage encountered. He also managed to capture a particularly colorful meteor as it blazed through the sky.

"One meteor was rather dramatic. It went through multiple colors as it traveled through the atmosphere," Gage continued.

Gage captured the photographs with a Nikon D5500 and a 14mm lens.

And the colorful displays weren't limited to North America.

In Japan, astronomer Daichi Fujii, curator of the Hiratsuka City Museum, captured a spectacular Leonid fireball streaking across the sky above Hiratsuka in the early hours of Nov. 19.

The brilliant fireball left behind a glowing trail that changed from green to orange as it lingered in the sky.

さきほど、しし座流星群の大火球が流れました。2026年11月19日4時35分2秒に、平塚から北の低い空に向けたカメラでとらえた様子です。緑色のアフターグローからオレンジ色の永続痕まで、美しく色を変化させました。 https://t.co/Q5ihqCPtX2November 18, 2026.

A fireball is defined as an unusually bright meteor that reaches a visual magnitude of -3 or brighter, according to NASA's Center for Near Earth Object Studies.

Elsewhere in Japan, skywatcher @simao had a particularly productive night, capturing an impressive 92 meteors between 10:17 p.m. local time on Nov. 18 and 5:40 a.m. on Nov. 19, from central Saitama Prefecture.

昨夜から今朝にかけて捉えた流星は正味92個でした。 11/18 22:17 〜 11/19 05:40 埼玉県中央から #atomcam #meteordetect #火球 #流星 https://t.co/jRzsHdQ7MVNovember 19, 2026.

Industry observers note that but that wasn't all simao captured that night! At 2:19 a.m. on Nov. 19, they caught both a Leonid meteor and a sprite at the same time, looking northwest.

Sprites are very difficult to capture, as they appear as fleeting flashes of light high above thunderstorms, typically appearing as red, jellyfish-like structures.

昨夜の流星とスプライト、初めて同じタイミングで撮れた。 11/19 02:19:36 埼玉県中央から北西の空 #atomcam #meteordetect #火球 #流星 #スプライト https://t.co/LBipTuoM0LNovember 19, 2026.

The Leonids were already making an appearance in the days leading up to the shower's peak.

Industry observers note that on Nov. 16, astrophotographer @EricTheSpaceCat captured several possible Leonids streaking through the sky.

Sources indicate that meteors from last night/this morning. Cropped to show detail. A lot of possible Leonids. The Leonid meteor shower is active and peaks the night of 11/17-11/18. https://t.co/s7YsvKdvECNovember 15, 2026.

Industry observers note that A likely Leonid meteor from yesterday morning. The Leonid meteor shower peaks tonight! Good luck if you go out to watch. https://t.co/xxbEV32NQlNovember 17, 2026.

If the Leonids have left you wanting more, you won't have to wait long for another significant meteor shower! Next up are the Geminids, one of the most prolific meteor showers of the year, which will peak overnight on Dec. 13-14. And 2026 is shaping up to be a particularly good year for them. With only a slender waxing crescent moon in the sky, moonlight interference will be minimal, giving skywatchers a chance to spot up to 120 Geminid meteors per hour under ideal conditions.

For the best views, head somewhere dark, away from city lights, and give your eyes around 30 minutes to adjust to the darkness.

Editor's Note: If you snap an impressive night sky photo and would like to share it with Space.com's readers, send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

Daisy Dobrijevic joined Space.com in February 2022, having previously worked as a staff writer for All About Space magazine. She completed an editorial internship with BBC Sky at Night Magazine and worked at the National Space Centre, communicating space science to the public.

Daisy holds a PhD in plant physiology and a Master's in Environmental Science. Based in Nottingham, U.K., she covers all things space, with a special focus on solar activity and space weather. She also has a keen interest in astrotourism and is always on the lookout for the next northern lights adventure.

She will join Hurtigruten as an onboard astronomer for a northern lights sailing in January 2027.

In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparations.

Recent findings suggest that I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group.

As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that germany, who finished top of Group A2 following their 5-0 win over the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday are to face Belgium in the Nations League quarterfinals — after they finished second in Group A1. The Belgians recently came up with a statement result of their own, beating Italy 4-1. The match-up between the neighboring countries promises to be closely contested, with Belgium sitting at No. 8 in the men's rankings, three places above Germany.

The head coach of Belgium is former Bayern Munich player Mark van Bommel, who took over from Rudi Garcia following the World Cup, where they were knocked out by eventual champions Spain in the quarterfinals.

Germany head into the knockout phase on a high note, not only because they won their group, but also the way they performed in their last two matches, against Serbia and the Netherlands in the group stage.

Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp followed the draw, held in Nyon on Friday, from the German FA's (DFB) Frankfurt offices. He played down the notion that Germany enter the tie as the favorites.

According to recent reports, "I've practically never given it any thought. It's never interested me," he mentioned.

"An awful lot can happen in that time. We're very happy with the final impression we left, yet we're also fully aware that we're only at the very beginning of a development process. We want to carry this positive momentum forward—there's still a great deal to be done.".

The matches are slated for March 25 and March 30, 2027, and having won their group, Germany will have home-field advantage for the second leg.

Germany and Belgium have faced each other 26 times to date, with West Germany and Germany having the upper hand with 20 wins, five defeats and one draw.

Should Germany advance to the semifinals, they will go on to face the winner of England and Norway, a World Cup quarterfinals rematch.

In the other two semifinals matchups, the Netherlands drew Portugal, while the top pairing sees Spain face France in a rematch of one of last summer's World Cup semifinals.

The "Final Four" mini tournament is to be held from June 9 to 13 but the host venue won't be determined until the semifinal lineup has been completed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Vitaly Janelt scored a spectacular 30-yard goal as Brentford cruised to an emphatic 4-0 victory against 10-man Everton at the Gtech Community Stadium.

A run of just one victory in five outings had caused early-season optimism surrounding Keith Andrews’ team to fade, but this was a resolute performance to propel them to sixth in the Premier League. Culpability for Everton’s collapse rested largely with James Tarkowski, sent off in the 40th minute following a dangerous challenge on Yehor Yarmolyuk.

In a recent development, david Moyes was setting a record for matches in charge of Everton, his 593rd game surpassing the historic tally set by Harry Catterick during the 1960s and 1970s. Yet a miserable opening half ensured it was an ordeal rather than a celebration.

It has been revealed that virtually everything went wrong for the visitors. Both of Brentford’s initial goals, scored by Keane Lewis-Potter, came via deflections, and Tarkowski’s temporary abandonment of responsibility - lunging studs-first into Yarmolyuk’s shin with his side two goals down - proved impossible for Moyes to mitigate. He was badly let down by a senior figure in a time of need.

It has been revealed that thereafter, the fixture offered little competition. The match might have drifted toward a standard two-goal victory for Brentford had Janelt not delivered a brilliant strike from distance that whistled past Jordan Pickford to compound the misery for Moyes and Tarkowski alike.

Fabio Carvalho turned the ball over the goal-line using his knee during stoppage time, providing the final indignity for Everton.

Brentford were impressive throughout. In the early stages, Callum Wilson picked out Michael Kayode making a run up the right side; the full-back was presented with a clear sight of Pickford’s goal but dragged his strike wide across the face.

Everton were making it far too easy. Midway through the half, they failed to cope with a ball over the top, allowing Jaidon Anthony to send a low pass into the middle with a deft touch. It was a controlled first-time delivery that found Lewis-Potter in space, his shot spinning in off Jarrad Branthwaite.

It required less than two minutes for Lewis-Potter to add a near-identical second, as a delivery into the box from Mikkel Damsgaard exposed fragile Everton defending.

The Brentford player was afforded two opportunities, his initial attempt rebounding back to him before squeezing the ball home at the second attempt via a deflection off Thierno Barry.

It has been revealed that everton were sinking and their captain abandoned them to their fate. Tarkowski was initially handed only a yellow card for a studs-up challenge on Yarmolyuk. 📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (466 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Empire State Building glowed in glittering gold last night (Nov.
  • EST (1016 GMT), NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hit one light-day from Earth.
  • To celebrate the major milestone for the farthest human-made object in history, the Empire State Building in Upcoming York City lit up in gold.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Empire State Building glowed in glittering gold last night (Nov. 17) to celebrate NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hitting one light-day from Earth. And it isn't the only building celebrating this achievement with a sparkling display.

Today (Nov. 18) at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT), NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hit one light-day from Earth. About 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers) away, this is the point at which it takes a full day (or 24 hours) for one light particle to get from us to the probe. So any signal we send to Voyager 1 or it sends back now takes a full day as the spacecraft continues to explore interstellar space.

To celebrate the major milestone for the farthest human-made object in history, the Empire State Building in Upcoming York City lit up in gold. This golden glow references the Golden Record onboard both the Voyager 1 and 2 spacecraft.

And the Empire State Building wasn't the only major landmark to celebrate the occasion. The Space Needle in Seattle, Washington, and both the Willis Tower and the Skydeck Chicago in Chicago, Illinois have all been illuminated gold to mark the milestone.

The Golden Record that these gold glowing buildings are referencing serves as an inanimate ambassador for Earth, carrying information about humanity, our planet, the other species who live here, the languages we speak, the music we listen to and so much more. It even includes instructions for building a record player to play the record.

In a recent development, the Voyager mission has, and continues to, make incredible scientific discoveries and observations throughout our solar system and now in interstellar space. But this Golden Record provides an additional aspect to the mission that connects us here on Earth to whatever unknown life may exist out there.

If some sort of life forms out in the cosmos were to ever come across Voyager and its Golden Record at any point in the distant future, they might learn a little bit about our small blue dot.

Chelsea Gohd served as a Senior Writer for Space.com from 2018 to 2022 before returning in 2026, covering everything from climate change to planetary science and human spaceflight in both articles and on-camera in videos. With a M.S. in Biology, Chelsea has written and worked for institutions including NASA JPL, the American Museum of Natural History, Scientific American, Discover Magazine Blog, Astronomy Magazine, and Live Science. When not writing, editing or filming something space-y, Gohd is writing music and performing as Foxanne, even launching a song to space in 2021 with Inspiration4. You can follow her online @chelsea.gohd and @foxanne.music.

#162481. Measles in America: Here's a constructive approach to beating the disease, based on Brazil's experience

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1380 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Measles in America: Here's a constructive approach to beating the disease, based on Brazil's experience

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1380 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that health experts saw it coming — the fact that after 26 years, the US would lose its status as measles-free.
  • On November 17, 2026, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) remarked the US had lost its measles elimination status, along with Mexico.
  • Look at Brazil, where in 2019, with more than 21,000 measles cases, the country also lost its measles-free status.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that health experts saw it coming — the fact that after 26 years, the US would lose its status as measles-free. Back in July 2026, DW reported how one epidemiologist had suggested an 'amnesia' about the measles risk was pushing a growth in US infections.

Four months later, it was official. On November 17, 2026, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) remarked the US had lost its measles elimination status, along with Mexico.

But it doesn't have to stay this way.

Look at Brazil, where in 2019, with more than 21,000 measles cases, the country also lost its measles-free status. But within five years — during the COVID-19 pandemic — it fought and won back its measles-free status. And since 2024, Brazil has stayed measles-free, even as the highly contagious disease spread across the rest of the Americas.

It has been revealed that in 2026, with the data available up to the time of writing this article, Brazil had only had 70 measles cases. They were all linked to infections brought in from abroad, often from neighboring Peru.

Industry observers note that brazil has fewer people than the US, about 213 million compared to the US's nearly 350 million, but the two countries are similar in size. So the comparison is worth considering.

Brazil moves fast. The PAHO asks countries to respond within 72 hours of a suspected measles case. Here's Brazil's own rule:.

Sources indicate that it has also made hunting for cases a national habit. In a program called "Dia S," health workers knock on doors and visit schools, daycare centers and churches to find people who may be sick but have not seen a doctor.

Brazil also holds mass vaccination days called "Dia D." There was one in November, in the area where Brazil borders Colombia and Peru.

If someone is diagnosed with measles, health workers try to track down every person the patient may have met ("contact persons") and vaccinate them and other people living nearby.

The country has so far provided more than 16 million doses of the measles vaccine in 2026 and has donated 500,000 doses to Peru.

Brazil isn't perfect, though. According to official estimates from the World Health Organization, only 76% of children got both required doses of the vaccine in 2025 — well short of the 95% target. Experts warn this leaves the country at risk because measles is so highly contagious. A country needs to be as close to 100% immunized as possible to protect people and stop the disease from spreading.

According to recent reports, "Elimination is not a trophy that we win once and put on a shelf. It must be protected every day," states PAHO Director Jarbas Barbosa.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The US lost its measles-free status because the PAHO found that the same strain of the virus had been spreading in the country for 12 months or more. Mexico and Bolivia lost their status on the same day as the US.

Industry observers note that the US has had more than 5,400 cases in 2026 (at time of writing), more than twice as many as in all of 2025, and about 19 times as many as in 2024. Nearly everyone who got sick with measles was unvaccinated or had an unknown vaccination status.

Industry observers note that US President Donald Trump signed an executive order on fresh vaccination recommendations for children in August 2026. It came at a time, when, as we reported, experts said people had stopped getting vaccinated against measles because infection rates were low. But like PAHO's Barbosa said, neglecting vaccination when infection rates are low is a mistake.

To be fair, Trump's executive order listed the measles vaccine in a top category of vaccinations recommended for every child. But the administration's stance on vaccination in general is unclear.

Industry observers note that health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has often declared opposition to vaccination, including against measles, advising people to take vitamin A instead. In Texas, this led to children being hospitalized with toxic levels of the supplement, and left them with no protection against measles.

Sources indicate that before the COVID-19 pandemic, 95% of US kindergartners had their measles shots. Now, it's 92%, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Protection (CDC). That leaves about 280,000 kindergartners in the US unprotected.

In the Texas counties where a 2025 measles outbreak began, coverage was as low as 77% at the time.

US children usually need vaccines to start school, but most states let parents opt out for religious or personal reasons, with no doctor involved.

But vaccination rates have fallen elsewhere in the world as well, including in Europe. In Germany, where measles infections have also risen, experts blame anti-vaccination rhetoric that emerged during the COVID-19 pandemic.

A person sick with measles can infect up to18 other, unprotected people. With vaccination, it is possible to increase the number of protected people and lower the number of people the sick person can infect.

According to recent reports, to prevent a measles outbreak, a community needs about 95% of people to be vaccinated and/or immune. The vaccination consists of two doses of the MMR (measles, mumps, rubella) vaccine.

But even after the two doses, a person can expect to have only 97% protection against measles — 3% short of full protection — so, nearly everyone in the community has to be vaccinated to keep the average level of protect as close to 100% as possible.

"For some diseases like measles, even a small decrease in vaccination rates can lead to more outbreaks of disease [so] community immunity requires over 95% of susceptible individuals to be immunized," says Andrew Racine, president of the American Academy of Pediatrics.

And the 95% has to hold everywhere. A good national average can be affected by, for example, a single school where only 70% of the children are vaccinated. And that is where the outbreak is likely to start.

Around the world, measles deaths have dropped by 88% since 2000, thanks to vaccines.

But progress has stalled. Only about three out of four children worldwide get both doses of the vaccine. The biggest outbreaks right now are in Bangladesh, Indonesia and Guatemala.

Sources indicate that data from Europe shows that things can get better. In the European Union, cases fell from more than 35,000 in 2024 to about 2,300 the following year, with no measles-related deaths.

Romania went from more than 30,000 cases in 2024 to about 4,200 in 2025.

In Hungary, where 99% of children are vaccinated, there have been no measles cases in the past year.

But in January, six European countries lost their measles-free status, including the UK, Spain and Austria. Across Europe, eight out of ten people who got measles in 2025 were unvaccinated.

The Americas are seeing a major surge in measles infections, with more than 58,000 cases in 2026, over four times as many as by November in 2025. Guatemala has been hit hardest, with almost 35,000 cases.

In a recent development, the deadliest outbreaks are in Africa. African Union countries have so far reported nearly 1,800 measles deaths in 2026, about 1,650 of them in Democratic Republic of Congo. Yet, Sudan, despite the war, raised first-dose measles coverage by 22 percentage points in 2025, which was the world's largest gain.

Sources indicate that measles is extremely contagious. One person can infect up to 18 unprotected people, which makes it about 12 times more contagious than the flu.

The virus can linger in the air for up to two hours after a sick person has left the room. And people spread it before they know they are sick. Someone with measles is contagious for four days before the rash appears and four days after.

It has been revealed that it's not just a rash. About one in five unvaccinated people who get measles in the US ends up in the hospital. Measles can weaken the immune system for years, making it harder to fight off other infections.

But it's preventable. Two doses of the MMR vaccine (which also protects against mumps and rubella) protect 97% of people for life.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that poxviruses enclose a complete viral transcription machinery alongside their dsDNA genome within the viral core, a transcription-competent compartment delimited by a permeable multi-layered protein shell.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that poxviruses enclose a complete viral transcription machinery alongside their dsDNA genome within the viral core, a transcription-competent compartment delimited by a permeable multi-layered protein shell. Upon infection of a cell and core release, this machinery almost immediately starts synthesizing early mRNAs, which are extruded across the core wall into the cytoplasm for translation. While in vitro structures of the isolated viral DNA-dependent RNA polymerase (vRNAP) have been described1–3, its native in virio architecture, spatial organization, and physical coupling to the genome remain unknown. Using cryo-electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging on purified Vaccinia virus cores, we reveal that packaged vRNAP exists not as monomer, but as massive 1.8 MDa resting-state dimer bridged by fully ordered vaccinia virus early transcription factor (VETF). We also identify a subpopulation of these dimers bound to the essential kinase VPK2 and the core protein L4, which directly tether the transcribing engines to the packaged genome near the inner core wall. Furthermore, we determine a sub-nanometer structure of the putative poxvirus mRNA extrusion portal complex, revealing a rigid assembly integrated into the core wall comprising an E8 hexameric crown, an E6 hexameric central hub, and a basal L3 dodecameric channel suited for nucleic acid export. Together, these structures provide a comprehensive architectural blueprint of important components of the poxvirus core and open upcoming structural and functional avenues for investigating poxvirus genome packaging, transcription activation, and mRNA extrusion.

Tonight’s opponents have taken nine points from their four matches, with wins over Villarreal, Sabah and Real Betis, but they suffered a shock 1-0 defeat at the hands of Bodo Glimt, to leave them 12th in the table.

The two sides have met eight times before, but their last meeting was back during the 2014/15 season when they were drawn together in the group stages.

Recent findings suggest that "3 Body Problem," Netflix's unsettling adaptation of the first book in Chinese author Cixin Liu's epic alien invasion trilogy, "Remembrance of Earth’s Past," made a serious impact on viewers searching for hardcore E.T. drama and now an explosive latest trailer for season 2 has just entered our orbit.

Recent findings suggest that this sensational saga about a malevolent interstellar society trying to exist within the unpredictable orbital mechanics of a planet and its triple sun system that forms an Earth-bound armada still has us a bit slack-jawed more than two years after debuting in 2024. Now we're admittedly eager for this shortened 6-episode sophomore outing, which is officially arriving on Jan. 14, 2027.

In a recent development, delivered by Emmy Award-winning "Game of Thrones" team of David Benioff and D.B. Weiss and "True Blood's" Alexander Woo, "3 Body Problem" season 2 revolves around the combined forces of the Planetary Defense Council as they mount a daring deep space counterattack against the San-Ti.

These Trisolarians are not the friendliest of galactic neighbors, and prior to the all-out invasion their primary goal was to thwart humanity’s ability to create advanced defense weaponry in the four centuries it would take for them to enter our solar system. This time it's more about the next phase of ultimate survival and dire actions taken by anti-alien and pro-alien factions.

Season 2 leaps forward 400 years and focuses on the results of the Wallfacer Project, a secret initiative where chosen individuals worked on solutions in isolation as to not attract the attention of the Trisolarian's omnipresent AI surveillance technology called sophons.

While the debut season was based on Liu's Hugo Award-winning 2008 novel, "The Three-Body Problem," this upcoming Netflix offering will adapt the second book, "The Dark Forest." 2010's "Death's End" closed out the acclaimed sci-fi trilogy.

In a recent development, "So much of season 1 is about the mystery of what's happening," co-creator and co-executive producer David Benioff tells Netflix. "By the time season 2 starts, we have a lot more information. We know there is a hostile alien civilization out there, the San-Ti, and they’re coming our way, and they want our planet for themselves.".

Industry observers note that landing on Jan. 14, 2027, "3 Body Problem" season 2's international cast includes returners Jess Hong, Benedict Wong, Jovan Adepo, Eiza González, Liam Cunningham, Marlo Kelly, Sea Shimooka, Saamer Usmani, Alex Sharp and Josh Brener. Joining them are fresh cast members Claudia Doumit, Ellie de Lange, Alfie Allen, David Yip and Jordan Sunshine.

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

League Two player Isiah Noel-Williams has been charged with three counts of rape.

Noel-Williams, who plays for Barnet, was remanded in custody as part of a police investigation by Hertfordshire Constabulary’s Public Protection Command, which has now confirmed charges against the footballer.

The 23-year-old from St Albans has also been charged with assault by penetration, engaging in sexual communication with a child, and supplying a controlled drug (Class B).

Noel-Williams appeared at Hatfield Magistrates’ Court on Saturday 21 November where he was taken into custody.

He will next appear at St Albans Crown Court on Tuesday 22 December.

Barnet put out a statement before the charges were made public, writing on their website: “The club is co-operating fully with the authorities and will determine any further action in due course.

“As this is now a matter for the courts, the club will not be making any further comment.”.

This season was Noel-Williams’ first in the Football League, joining Barnet from non-league side Hemel Hempstead in the summer.

The striker has made nine appearances across all competitions and is yet to register a goal contribution.

He has previously played for a number of non-league clubs including Kettering Town, Matlock Town and Harrow Borough.

Noel-Williams was sent off in a 1-1 draw with Oldham in October, with manager Dean Brennan branding the red card a “farce”, and he subsequently received racist abuse which Barnet condemned “in the strongest terms”.

Barnet are vying for promotion this term and sit second in League Two, trailing leaders Salford City by four points.

Tech Report: Don't miss Saturn shine close to the moon tonight

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (403 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the moon shines close to the ringed giant Saturn after sunset tonight (Nov.
  • Recent findings suggest that saturn's steady light will appear a little over 5 degrees from the 82%-lit moon in the southeastern sky after the sun dips below the horizon for viewers in the U.S.
  • Moonlight will hide fainter stars from view, though you should be able to spot Algenib, Markab, Alpheratz and Scheat arrayed in a diamond formation above the lunar disk, marking out the asterism of the Great Square of Pegasus in the November sky.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the moon shines close to the ringed giant Saturn after sunset tonight (Nov. 20), presenting a spectacular naked-eye display as the stars of the Great Square of Pegasus twinkle nearby.

Recent findings suggest that saturn's steady light will appear a little over 5 degrees from the 82%-lit moon in the southeastern sky after the sun dips below the horizon for viewers in the U.S. — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length.

Moonlight will hide fainter stars from view, though you should be able to spot Algenib, Markab, Alpheratz and Scheat arrayed in a diamond formation above the lunar disk, marking out the asterism of the Great Square of Pegasus in the November sky.

The moon will present a spectacular target through the eyepiece of a 6-inch telescope, as the terminator line separating night from day creeps ever closer to its western edge. It's a great time to explore the 110 km-wide Gassendi Crater on the edge of Mare Humorum as its eastern rim and central peaks throw intense shadows across its interior.

Slewing your telescope over to Saturn will reveal details and subtle variations in the cloud surface of the gas giant, along with its iconic ring system, which is gradually becoming more visible following its ring plane crossing in March 2025.

Depending on viewing conditions, you may also notice a shoal of bright, star-like points of light surrounding Saturn's disk, which represent the large moons Titan, Dione, Tethys, Rhea and Iapetus.

In a recent development, interested in seeing the planets of the solar system up close for yourself? Then be sure to check out our picks of the best telescopes available in 2026, including the Celestron NexStar 8SE, which we rate as the best motorized scope out there.
